objects.name: CMK_APPL_PARTNERS_SETUP_VL
objects.query:
WITH OPT_IN_ENABLED AS (
SELECT 1 FROM DUAL WHERE RCS_INTERFACE.CONVERT_IS_FEATURE_ENABLED_BOOLEAN_TO_CHAR('COMBO','ORA_CMK_B2B_DOCUMENT_SETUP') = 'Y'
),
DOCUMENT_ENABLED AS (
SELECT 1
FROM CMK_DOC_PROPERTY_VALUES DPV
WHERE DPV.DOC_PROPERTY_ID IN (
SELECT DP.DOC_PROPERTY_ID
FROM CMK_DOC_PROPERTIES DP
WHERE DP.DOCUMENT_ID = 40076
AND DP.PROPERTY_CODE = 'ORA_ENABLED_FLAG'
)
AND DPV.VALUE = 'Y'
),
DEFAULT_CONN_ENABLED AS (
SELECT 1
FROM CMK_DECISION_TABLE_DETAILS DTD
JOIN CMK_DECISION_TABLE_HEADERS DTH
ON DTD.HEADER_ID = DTH.HEADER_ID
WHERE DTH.CONTEXT1 = 40076
AND DTH.CONTEXT2 = 'DEFAULT'
AND DTD.STATUS = 'ORA_CMK_CONN_ENABLED'
)
SELECT DISTINCT
DTD.HEADER_ID AS APPL_PARTNER_ID,
'Supplier Site' AS PARTNER_KEY_TYPE,
JSON_VALUE(DTD.DATA, '$.SupplierId') AS PARTNER_KEY1,
JSON_VALUE(DTD.DATA, '$.SupplierSiteId') AS PARTNER_KEY2,
JSON_VALUE(DTD.DATA, '$.SupplierName') AS PARTNER_KEY3,
JSON_VALUE(DTD.DATA, '$.SupplierNumber') AS PARTNER_KEY4,
JSON_VALUE(DTD.DATA, '$.SupplierSiteName') AS PARTNER_KEY5,
CPP.APPL_PARTNER_CODE AS PROC_ACTION_CODE,
NULL AS EXTERNAL_PARTNER_ID,
CEPM.PROVIDER_ID AS SERVICE_PROVIDER_ID,
CEPM.DOCUMENT_ID AS DOCUMENT_ID,
CEPM.PARTNER_MESSAGE_ID AS PARTNER_MESSAGE_ID,
CEPM.PARTNER_MESSAGE_NAME AS PARTNER_MESSAGE_NAME,
DTD.DETAIL_ID AS APPL_PARTNER_DOC_ID,
DTD.STATUS AS APPL_PARTNER_DOC_STATUS,
'Y' AS PRIMARY_RECIPIENT_FLAG,
CDM.DELIVERY_METHOD_ID AS DELIVERY_METHOD_ID,
CDM.DELIVERY_METHOD_TYPE AS DELIVERY_METHOD_TYPE,
CDM.RECIPIENT_EMAIL_ID AS RECIPIENT_EMAIL_ID,
CEPMC.OVERRIDE_STATUS AS OVERRIDE_STATUS
FROM CMK_DECISION_TABLE_DETAILS DTD
JOIN CMK_DECISION_TABLE_HEADERS DTH
ON DTD.HEADER_ID = DTH.HEADER_ID
JOIN CMK_EXTERNAL_PTNR_MSGS_B CEPM
ON JSON_VALUE(DTD.DATA, '$.ConnectionId') = CEPM.PARTNER_MESSAGE_ID
JOIN CMK_EXT_PTNR_MSGS_CUST CEPMC
ON CEPM.PARTNER_MESSAGE_ID = CEPMC.PARTNER_MESSAGE_CUST_ID
JOIN CMK_DELIVERY_METHODS CDM
ON CEPMC.DELIVERY_METHOD_ID = CDM.DELIVERY_METHOD_ID
LEFT JOIN CMK_PARTNER_PROPERTIES CPP
ON CPP.PARTNER_KEY1 = JSON_VALUE(DTD.DATA, '$.SupplierId')
AND CPP.PARTNER_KEY2 = JSON_VALUE(DTD.DATA, '$.SupplierSiteId')
WHERE DTH.CONTEXT1 = 40076
AND DTH.CONTEXT2 = 'SUPPLIER_SITE'
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM OPT_IN_ENABLED)
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM DOCUMENT_ENABLED)
UNION ALL
SELECT DTD.HEADER_ID AS APPL_PARTNER_ID,
'Default' AS PARTNER_KEY_TYPE,
TO_CHAR(SUPPLIERPEO.VENDOR_ID) AS PARTNER_KEY1,
TO_CHAR(SUPPLIERSITEDPEO.VENDOR_SITE_ID) AS PARTNER_KEY2,
PARTYPEO.PARTY_NAME AS PARTNER_KEY3,
SUPPLIERPEO.SEGMENT1 AS PARTNER_KEY4,
SUPPLIERSITEDPEO.VENDOR_SITE_CODE AS PARTNER_KEY5,
NULL AS PROC_ACTION_CODE,
NULL AS EXTERNAL_PARTNER_ID,
CEPM.PROVIDER_ID AS SERVICE_PROVIDER_ID,
CEPM.DOCUMENT_ID AS DOCUMENT_ID,
CEPM.PARTNER_MESSAGE_ID AS PARTNER_MESSAGE_ID,
CEPM.PARTNER_MESSAGE_NAME AS PARTNER_MESSAGE_NAME,
DTD.DETAIL_ID AS APPL_PARTNER_DOC_ID,
DTD.STATUS AS APPL_PARTNER_DOC_STATUS,
'Y' AS PRIMARY_RECIPIENT_FLAG,
CDM.DELIVERY_METHOD_ID AS DELIVERY_METHOD_ID,
CDM.DELIVERY_METHOD_TYPE AS DELIVERY_METHOD_TYPE,
CDM.RECIPIENT_EMAIL_ID AS RECIPIENT_EMAIL_ID,
CEPMC.OVERRIDE_STATUS AS OVERRIDE_STATUS
FROM HZ_PARTIES PARTYPEO,
POZ_SUPPLIERS SUPPLIERPEO,
HZ_PARTY_SITES PARTYSITEPEO,
POZ_SUPPLIER_SITES_ALL_M SUPPLIERSITEDPEO,
FUN_BU_USAGES_V BUSINESSUNITUSAGEPEO,CMK_DECISION_TABLE_DETAILS DTD
JOIN CMK_DECISION_TABLE_HEADERS DTH
ON DTD.HEADER_ID = DTH.HEADER_ID
JOIN CMK_EXTERNAL_PTNR_MSGS_B CEPM
ON JSON_VALUE(DTD.DATA,
'$.ConnectionId') = CEPM.PARTNER_MESSAGE_ID
JOIN CMK_EXT_PTNR_MSGS_CUST CEPMC
ON CEPM.PARTNER_MESSAGE_ID = CEPMC.PARTNER_MESSAGE_CUST_ID
JOIN CMK_DELIVERY_METHODS CDM
ON CEPMC.DELIVERY_METHOD_ID = CDM.DELIVERY_METHOD_ID
WHERE DTH.CONTEXT1 = 40076
AND DTH.CONTEXT2 = 'DEFAULT'
AND PARTYPEO.PARTY_ID = SUPPLIERPEO.PARTY_ID
AND PARTYPEO.PARTY_ID = PARTYSITEPEO.PARTY_ID
AND SUPPLIERPEO.VENDOR_ID = SUPPLIERSITEDPEO.VENDOR_ID
AND SUPPLIERSITEDPEO.PARTY_SITE_ID = PARTYSITEPEO.PARTY_SITE_ID
AND SUPPLIERSITEDPEO.PRC_BU_ID = BUSINESSUNITUSAGEPEO.BUSINESS_UNIT_ID
AND SUPPLIERSITEDPEO.B2B_COMM_METHOD_CODE = 'CMK'
AND PARTYPEO.PARTY_TYPE = 'ORGANIZATION'
AND BUSINESSUNITUSAGEPEO.STATUS = 'A'
AND BUSINESSUNITUSAGEPEO.MODULE_KEY = 'PROCUREMENT_BF'
AND ( SUPPLIERPEO.VENDOR_ID,
SUPPLIERSITEDPEO.VENDOR_SITE_ID ) NOT IN (
SELECT DISTINCT JSON_VALUE(DTD.DATA,
'$.SupplierId') AS VENDOR_ID,
JSON_VALUE(DTD.DATA,
'$.SupplierSiteId') AS VENDOR_SITE_ID
FROM CMK_DECISION_TABLE_DETAILS DTD,
CMK_DECISION_TABLE_HEADERS DTH
WHERE DTD.HEADER_ID = DTH.HEADER_ID
AND DTH.CONTEXT1 = 40076
AND DTH.CONTEXT2 = 'SUPPLIER_SITE'
)
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM DEFAULT_CONN_ENABLED)
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM OPT_IN_ENABLED)
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM DOCUMENT_ENABLED)
UNION ALL
SELECT
CMK_APPLICATION_PARTNERS.APPL_PARTNER_ID,
CMK_APPLICATION_PARTNERS.PARTNER_KEY_TYPE,
CMK_APPLICATION_PARTNERS.PARTNER_KEY1,
CMK_APPLICATION_PARTNERS.PARTNER_KEY2,
CMK_APPLICATION_PARTNERS.PARTNER_KEY3,
CMK_APPLICATION_PARTNERS.PARTNER_KEY4,
CMK_APPLICATION_PARTNERS.PARTNER_KEY5,
CMK_APPLICATION_PARTNERS.PROC_ACTION_CODE,
CMK_APPLICATION_PARTNERS.EXTERNAL_PARTNER_ID,
CMK_APPLICATION_PARTNERS.SERVICE_PROVIDER_ID,
CMK_APPL_PARTNER_DOCS.DOCUMENT_ID,
CMK_EXTERNAL_PTNR_MSGS_B.PARTNER_MESSAGE_ID,
CMK_EXTERNAL_PTNR_MSGS_B.PARTNER_MESSAGE_NAME,
CMK_APPL_PARTNER_DOCS.APPL_PARTNER_DOC_ID,
CMK_APPL_PARTNER_DOCS.APPL_PARTNER_DOC_STATUS,
CMK_APPL_PARTNER_DOCS.PRIMARY_RECIPIENT_FLAG,
CMK_DELIVERY_METHODS.DELIVERY_METHOD_ID,
CMK_DELIVERY_METHODS.DELIVERY_METHOD_TYPE,
CMK_DELIVERY_METHODS.RECIPIENT_EMAIL_ID,
CMK_EXT_PTNR_MSGS_CUST.OVERRIDE_STATUS
FROM CMK_APPLICATION_PARTNERS
JOIN CMK_APPL_PARTNER_DOCS
ON CMK_APPLICATION_PARTNERS.APPL_PARTNER_ID = CMK_APPL_PARTNER_DOCS.APPL_PARTNER_ID
JOIN CMK_EXTERNAL_PTNR_MSGS_B
ON CMK_APPL_PARTNER_DOCS.DOCUMENT_ID = CMK_EXTERNAL_PTNR_MSGS_B.DOCUMENT_ID
JOIN CMK_EXT_PTNR_MSGS_CUST
ON CMK_EXTERNAL_PTNR_MSGS_B.PARTNER_MESSAGE_ID = CMK_EXT_PTNR_MSGS_CUST.PARTNER_MESSAGE_CUST_ID
JOIN CMK_DELIVERY_METHODS
ON CMK_EXT_PTNR_MSGS_CUST.DELIVERY_METHOD_ID = CMK_DELIVERY_METHODS.DELIVERY_METHOD_ID
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM OPT_IN_ENABLED)
AND (
CMK_APPLICATION_PARTNERS.EXTERNAL_PARTNER_ID = CMK_EXTERNAL_PTNR_MSGS_B.EXTERNAL_PARTNER_ID
OR (
CMK_APPLICATION_PARTNERS.SERVICE_PROVIDER_ID = CMK_EXTERNAL_PTNR_MSGS_B.SERVICE_PROVIDER_ID
AND CMK_EXTERNAL_PTNR_MSGS_B.EXTERNAL_PARTNER_ID IS NULL
AND NOT EXISTS (
SELECT 1
FROM CMK_EXTERNAL_PTNR_MSGS_B CMKEXTERNALPTNRMSGS
WHERE CMKEXTERNALPTNRMSGS.EXTERNAL_PARTNER_ID = CMK_APPLICATION_PARTNERS.EXTERNAL_PARTNER_ID
AND CMKEXTERNALPTNRMSGS.DOCUMENT_ID = CMK_EXTERNAL_PTNR_MSGS_B.DOCUMENT_ID
)
)
)

objects.name: WIE_CONFRM_CHECK_DETAILS
objects.description: This table stores the conformance check results details for primary products.

columns.name: CONFRM_CHECK_DETAIL_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a conformance result detail record. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: CONFRM_CHECK_RESULT_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a conformance check result that is a foreign key to WIS_CONFRM_CHECK_RESULTS table.

columns.name: LATEST_SIMULATION_FLAG
columns.comments: Indicates whether this record corresponds to the most recent simulation of the conformance check.

columns.name: SIMULATION_FLAG
columns.comments: Indicates whether the conformance check was executed in simulation mode.

columns.name: CONFRM_PARAM_TARGET_VALUE_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of the conformance parameter target value used for the conformance check that is the foreign key to WIS_CONFRM_PARAM_TARGET_VALUES table.

columns.name: CONFORMANCE_PARAMETER_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a conformance parameter that is the foreign key to WIS_CONFRM_PARAMETERS_B table.

columns.name: CONFRM_CHECK_RESULT_RUN_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of the conformance check execution instance.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of the work order associated with the conformance check result.

columns.name: INVENTORY_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of the item being evaluated for conformance check.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: The organization identifier that represents the manufacturing plant for which conformance check was performed.

columns.name: TARGET_VALUE
columns.comments: User-defined target value of the associated conformance parameter for a specific item.

columns.name: MIN_TARGET_VALUE
columns.comments: Minimum value of the associated conformance parameter for a specific item used for evaluating the conformance check criteria.

columns.name: MAX_TARGET_VALUE
columns.comments: Maximum value of the associated conformance parameter for a specific item used for evaluating the conformance check criteria.

columns.name: DATA_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates the data type used to evaluate the conformance parameter. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_CONFRM_PARAM_DATA_TYPE.

columns.name: DECIMAL_PRECISION
columns.comments: Number of digits allowed to the right of the decimal point for the associated conformance parameter.

columns.name: CALCULATED_VALUE
columns.comments: Indicates the measured value obtained during the conformance check execution.

columns.name: CONFORMANCE_CHECK_RESULT_DATE
columns.comments: Indicates the date on which the conformance check was performed.

columns.name: CONFRM_CHECK_RESULT_STATUS
columns.comments: Indicates the status of the conformance check. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_CONFORMANCE_STATUS_TYPE.

columns.name: QUANTITY
columns.comments: Indicates the quantity of the primary product for which conformance check is being performed on.

columns.name: UOM_CODE
columns.comments: The unit of measure code for the quantity of the primary product.

columns.name: QUANTITY_CONFORMANCE_PARAMETER
columns.comments: Indicates the converted quantity taking into consideration the conformance parameter data type.

columns.name: UOM_CODE_CONFORMANCE_PARAMETER
columns.comments: Indicates the unit of measure code of the conformance parameter taking into consideration the data type.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

objects.name: WIE_CONFRM_CHECK_ERRORS
objects.description: This table stores the conformance check errors.

columns.name: CONFRM_CHECK_ERROR_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a conformance error record. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: CONFRM_CHECK_DETAIL_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a conformance result detail record. Its value is the foreign key to WIE_CONFRM_CHECK_DETAILS table.

columns.name: CONFRM_CHECK_INGR_DTL_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a conformance ingredient detail record. Its value is the foreign key to WIE_CONFRM_CHECK_INGR_DTLS table.

columns.name: ERROR_CODE
columns.comments: Indicates the error code generated during the conformance check process, if any validation error occurred.

columns.name: ERROR_TOKEN_NAMES
columns.comments: Concatenated string of token names for the error message.

columns.name: ERROR_TOKEN_VALUES
columns.comments: Concatenated string of token values for the error message.

columns.name: CONFRM_CHECK_RESULT_RUN_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of the conformance check execution instance. This column links the record to the specific run in which the conformance error was reported.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

objects.description: This table stores the batch information for grouping interface records. An interface batch identifies the source system that the records are being interfaced from. columns.comments: Represents the identifier of the source system. If the source system type = "INTERNAL" this value equates to the application id. If "EXTERNAL", then it is the source system as defined in the trading community (TCA) source systems table.

When a service writes this record it will be WEB_SERVICE, and if batch records are created by the UI then it will be USER_INTERFACE. objects.name: WIE_MATERIAL_DISPENSE_DETAILS
objects.description: This table stores detailed material dispensing information, including dispense mode, source and target container details, measurements, and dispensed quantities, to support traceability and audit reporting.

columns.name: MATERIAL_DISPENSE_DETAIL_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a material dispensing transaction details. Its value is unique id generated from a sequence.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: MATERIAL_DISPENSE_ID
columns.comments: References the material dispense transaction for which the details are recorded.

columns.name: DISPENSE_MODE
columns.comments: Indicates the material dispense mode. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_MD_DISPENSE_MODES.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: Indicates the plant in which the material dispense transaction is created.

columns.name: SOURCE_CONTAINER_ID
columns.comments: Indicates the item identifier of the source container being used.

columns.name: SOURCE_CONTAINER_TARE
columns.comments: Indicates the tare weight associated to the source container being used. It is defaulted from the item master.

columns.name: SOURCE_CONTAINER_MEASURE
columns.comments: Indicates the measure of the source container including its contents before dispensing material.

columns.name: SOURCE_CONTAINER_REMEASURE
columns.comments: Indicates the measure of the source container including its contents after dispensing material.

columns.name: TARGET_CONTAINER_ID
columns.comments: Indicates the item identifier of the target container being used.

columns.name: TARGET_CONTAINER_TARE
columns.comments: Indicates the tare measure of the target container being used. It is defaulted from the item master. It can be modified during measuring process before dispensing material.

columns.name: TARGET_CONTAINER_MEASURE
columns.comments: Indicates the measure of the target container including its contents after dispensing material.

columns.name: DISPENSE_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Indicates the net dispense quantity. This is calculated based on the source and target measures after dispensing material.

columns.name: PRIMARY_DISPENSE_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Indicates the net dispense quantity in primary UOM of the material. This is calculated based on the source and target measures after dispensing materials.

columns.name: LOSS_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Indicates the net quantity lost during the process of being dispensed.

columns.name: PRIMARY_LOSS_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Indicates the net quantity lost during the process of being dispensed in primary UOM.

columns.name: SOURCE_MEASURE_SCALE_ID
columns.comments: Indicates the scale used for measuring source container while dispensing material. Represents foreign key to WIS_DISPENSE_SCALES.

columns.name: TARGET_MEASURE_SCALE_ID
columns.comments: Indicates the scale used for measuring target container while dispensing material. Represents foreign key to WIS_DISPENSE_SCALES.

objects.name: WIE_MATERIAL_DISPENSE_TASKS
objects.description: This table stores snapshot of instruction tasks completed as part of dispensing. This data will be used to show task details against completed dispense transactions in UI and reports.

columns.name: MATERIAL_DISPENSE_TASK_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a material dispensing instruction task. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: MATERIAL_DISPENSE_ID
columns.comments: Identifier of the material dispensing transaction for which the instruction task is performed.

columns.name: TASK_ID
columns.comments: Identifies the instruction task detail for the dispense instruction. This is a foreign key to PER_TASKS_IN_CHECKLIST_B.

columns.name: TASK_NAME
columns.comments: Name of the specific task performed as part of dispense instructions.

columns.name: TASK_TYPE
columns.comments: Task type defined in the dispense instruction template for the task. Valid values exist in lookup with lookup type = ORA_PER_CHK_TASK_ACTION_TYPE.

columns.name: MANDATORY_FLAG
columns.comments: Indicates if the task is optional or mandatory.

columns.name: TASK_SEQUENCE
columns.comments: Sequence in which the tasks are expected to be completed as part of dispense instructions.

columns.name: STATUS
columns.comments: Indicates the status of the task. Valid values exist in lookup with lookup type = PER_CHECKLIST_TASK_STATUS.

columns.name: TASK_COMMENTS
columns.comments: Comments entered by the user while completing the specific task.

columns.name: TASK_START_TIME
columns.comments: Time at which the task was started.

columns.name: TASK_END_TIME
columns.comments: Time at which the task was completed.

columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

objects.name: WIE_MATERIAL_TRANSACTIONS_INT
objects.description: This is the interface table for work order material transactions. Production progress updates, in terms of material consumption and production, are interfaced from either third party systems or from contract manufacturers via this interface table. All material transactions are eventually sent as inventory updates and reservation changes to Logistics.

columns.name: INTERFACE_ROW_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a material transaction interface record. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: INTERFACE_BATCH_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the user identified code for the interface batch.

columns.name: INTERFACE_BATCH_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal interface batch identifier. This is used to group a batch of interface records for processing. When interface records are brought in via services or the UI, the system will internally generate this value.

columns.name: INTERFACE_STATUS_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the progress of the interface processing with statuses such as ready for processing or currently in process as well as the various flavors of completion statuses. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_INTERFACE_STATUS.

columns.name: TXN_HEADER_NUMBER
columns.comments: This is a user loaded key that uniquely identifies the transaction within the batch. This user key will be used as a handle to connect the child entities (i.e. the WIE_TRANSACTION_LOTS_INT and WIE_TRANSACTION_SERIALS_INT tables) to this parent transaction table.

columns.name: PARENT_HEADER_NUMBER
columns.comments: This is a user loaded key that is used to allow reporting of lot or serial controlled components to an orderless transaction. This field will link the material transaction record to the orderless transaction record to create the parent/child relationship.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_CODE
columns.comments: The organization code that represents the manufacturing plant to which this material transaction is performed.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: The organization identifier that represents the manufacturing plant to which this material transaction is performed.

columns.name: WORK_CENTER_ID
columns.comments: The identifier of the work center to which this material transaction is being performed. This is an internally derived column for the purpose of transferring data to inventory.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_NUMBER
columns.comments: Represents the user-facing identifier of the work order. Material transactions are always performed in the context of a work order.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal identifier of the work order. Material transactions are always performed in the context of a work order.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates the type of this work order. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_WO_TYPE.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_SUB_TYPE
columns.comments: The subtype will be populated for non-standard work. This is used to derive the appropriate costing account for non-standard work. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_WO_SUB_TYPE.

columns.name: WO_OPERATION_SEQ_NUMBER
columns.comments: Represents the work order operation sequence from which this material transaction is being performed.

columns.name: WO_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: The internal identifier of the operation from which the primary product quantity is transacted.

columns.name: WO_MATERIAL_SEQ_NUMBER
columns.comments: Work Order Operation Material Sequence Number

columns.name: INVENTORY_ITEM_NUMBER
columns.comments: The user key for the inventory item number.

columns.name: INVENTORY_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: The primary product identifier defined on the work order. This is an internal column and is de-normalized.

columns.name: ITEM_REVISION
columns.comments: Revision of the item when the item is revision controlled.

columns.name: OUTPUT_TYPE
columns.comments: Type of output produced by the operation. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_WD_OUTPUT_MATERIAL.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_TYPE_CODE
columns.comments: Defines the nature of the material transaction. Valid values are listed in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_MTL_TXN_TYPE.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_DATE
columns.comments: Date when the material transaction is performed.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Material quantity that is being transacted.

columns.name: REQUIRED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Material quantity that is required for pull components or orderless transactions.

columns.name: ISSUED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the previously issued quantity based on an aggregation of data from the INV_MATERIAL_TXNS table. This is a calculated column used by the UI to quickly display the previously issued quantity.

columns.name: BASIS_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates whether the item quantity is fixed (i.e. quantity per lot produced) or variable (i.e. quantity per item produced). Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = EGP_BOM_BASIS_TYPE.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure code of the material quantity being transacted.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_UNIT_OF_MEASURE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure of the material quantity being transacted.

columns.name: SECONDARY_TRANSACTION_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the secondary quantity for a material transaction if the item is dual UOM enabled.

columns.name: SECONDARY_UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the secondary UOM for a material transaction if the item is dual UOM enabled.

columns.name: SECONDARY_UNIT_OF_MEASURE
columns.comments: Represents the secondary unit of measure for a material transaction if the item is dual UOM enabled.

columns.name: REASON_CODE
columns.comments: Indicates the reason code for the material transaction. Primarily used when material is being scrapped.

columns.name: REASON_ID
columns.comments: Represents the identifier of the material transaction reason. Primarily used when material is being scrapped. It is a foreign key to the INV_TRANSACTION_REASONS_B table.

columns.name: SUBINVENTORY_CODE
columns.comments: Subinventory where the material is drawn from or where the products are completed.

columns.comments: Represents the work method code for which this material transaction is applicable.

columns.name: WORK_METHOD_ID
columns.comments: Represents the work method for which this material transaction is applicable. It is a foreign key to the WIS_WORK_METHODS_B table.

columns.comments: Represents the user key to the work definition.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_ID
columns.comments: Represents the work definition identifier which is a foreign key to the WIS_WORK_DEFINITIONS table.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_VERSION
columns.comments: Represents the user key of the work definition version.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_VERSION_ID
columns.comments: Represents the work definition version identifier which is a foreign key to the WIS_WD_VERSIONS table.

columns.name: SOLD_TO_LEGAL_ENTITY_ID
columns.comments: The legal entity identifier of the enterprise that is procuring goods/services from the supplier.

columns.name: SOLD_TO_LEGAL_ENTITY_NAME
columns.comments: The legal entity name of the enterprise that is procuring goods/services from the supplier.

columns.name: PO_NUMBER
columns.comments: The user key to the Fusion Purchase Order Number.

columns.name: PO_HEADER_ID
columns.comments: The Fusion Purchase Order Identifier. The system key.

columns.name: PO_LINE_NUMBER
columns.comments: The Fusion Purchase Order Line Number. The user key.

columns.name: PO_LINE_ID
columns.comments: The Fusion Purchase Order Line Number. The system key identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_SYSTEM_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates the type of source system (i.e. internal or external) from which data is being imported. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_SOURCE_SYSTEM_TYPE.

columns.name: SOURCE_SYSTEM_ID
columns.comments: Represents the identifier of the source system. If the source system type = "INTERNAL" this value equates to the application id. If "EXTERNAL", then it is the source system as defined in the trading community (TCA) source systems table.

columns.name: SOURCE_SYSTEM_CODE
columns.comments: A code used to indicate the source system from which data is being imported. Depending on the source system type, this value could represent an internal Fusion product code or the actual trading community (TCA) source system reference.

columns.name: SOURCE_HEADER_REF
columns.comments: Represents the source system's user-facing header reference identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_HEADER_REF_ID
columns.comments: Represents the source system's internal header reference identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_LINE_REF
columns.comments: Represents the source system's user-facing line reference identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_LINE_REF_ID
columns.comments: Represents the source system's internal line reference identifier.

columns.name: WO_OP_TXN_INTERFACE_ROW_ID
columns.comments: This is an internal column that is used to link backflush material transaction interface records to an associated operation transaction interface record.

columns.name: WO_OPERATION_TRANSACTION_ID
columns.comments: To complete the interface cycle, the operation transaction processor updates the operation_transaction_id in this table after successfully processing the transactions.

columns.name: ASSEMBLY_SERIAL_NUMBER
columns.comments: The parent assembly serial number for which the material transaction is performed.

columns.name: ASSET_ID
columns.comments: The reference to the component asset when the material issued or returned is tracked in the asset repository.

columns.name: PARENT_ASSET_ID
columns.comments: Parent asset identifier of the component that is being removed or installed.

columns.name: PARENT_LOT_NUMBER
columns.comments: The lot number for the parent asset on which the material is issued to or returned from.

columns.name: PARENT_SERIAL_NUMBER
columns.comments: Parent serial number of the component that is being removed or installed.

columns.name: PARENT_INVENTORY_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: Parent item of the component that is being removed or installed.

columns.name: DEFER_GEN_RELATIONSHIP_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag indicating that the relationship processing in the MFG->ALM genealogy integration are to be deferred.

columns.name: INV_TRANSACTION_INTERFACE_ID
columns.comments: This is the identifier of the record that is written into the INV_TRANSACTIONS_INTERFACE table to process the completion (or the return) material transaction.

columns.name: INV_TRANSACTION_HEADER_ID
columns.comments: This is the TRANSACTION_HEADER_ID that we populate in INV_TRANSACTIONS_INTERFACE. This acts as a group handle in invoking the online inventory API. When the move transaction process is also writing backflush component consumption records in INV_TRANSACTIONS_INTERFACE, we will populate the same TRANSACTION_HEADER_ID value for the backflush transaction.

columns.name: INV_TRANSACTION_BATCH_ID
columns.comments: This is an internal inventory interface identifier that can be used to group logical transactions that must be processed in a logical unit. This controls the behavior of whether the logical unit should be processed together as a set. This column is used for internal processing.

columns.name: INV_TRANSACTION_ID
columns.comments: Upon successful processing of the material transaction by the inventory material transaction process online API, we record the successful INV_MATERIAL_TXNS.TRANSACTION_ID in this column. The INV online API returns this value.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_NOTE
columns.comments: This column is exclusive to the work orderless completion transaction. This note is captured upon performing the orderless completion/return/scrap transactions. This note is assigned to the last operation transaction that is created based on the work definition data. Users will be able to review operation transactions and the last operation transaction for orderless completions will contain this transaction note.

columns.name: TXN_SORT_ORDER
columns.comments: This is an internal column used by the Material Transaction train stop in the Dispatch List UI and Work Order Less Completion UI. The internal routine that gathers the backflush materials (both issue and return) materials that are tied to the operation transaction populates this column with a sequence number that is used when displaying the material rows on the UI.

columns.name: WORKER_ID
columns.comments: The partition number for multi-threading.

columns.name: USE_COMMON_INVENTORY_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag to determine whether material should be issued/returned from common inventory or from the project associated with the work order. A value of Y indicates material should be issued/returned from common inventory. A value of N indicates material should be issued/returned from the project associated with the work order.

columns.name: PJC_PROJECT_ID
columns.comments: Identifier of the project used to build the transaction descriptive flexfield for project-related transaction distributions. Foreign key to PJF_PROJECTS_ALL_B.PROJECT_ID.

columns.name: PJC_PROJECT_NUMBER
columns.comments: The number assigned to a project.

columns.name: PJC_TASK_ID
columns.comments: Identifier of the task used to build the transaction descriptive flexfield for project-related transaction distributions. Foreign key to PJF_PROJ_ELEMENTS_B.PROJ_ELEMENT_ID (however uses an alias of TASK_ID).

columns.name: PJC_TASK_NUMBER
columns.comments: The identifying number for a task which is a subdivision of project work.

columns.name: INV_STRIPING_CATEGORY
columns.comments: Segment used to identify the descriptive flexfield application context for Inventory striping attributes.

columns.name: PROJECT_ID
columns.comments: Identifier of the project used to stripe Inventory transactions.

columns.name: TASK_ID
columns.comments: Identifier of the task used to stripe Inventory transactions.

objects.name: WIE_MA_EXPECTED_SUPPLIES
objects.description: The table stores the information related to the expected supplies of materials.

columns.name: MA_EXPECTED_SUPPLY_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a material availability expected supplies record. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: INVENTORY_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: Represents the item for which the expected supply is being calculated.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: The organization identifier that represents the manufacturing plant to which this item belongs.

columns.name: SOURCE_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates the source from where the item is expected. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_MA_EXP_SOURCE_TYPE.

columns.name: SOURCE_HEADER_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal identifier of the source header reference where the supply is expected.

columns.name: SOURCE_NUMBER
columns.comments: Represents the user-facing identifier of the source header reference where the supply is expected. Examples include the purchase order number or the work order number.

columns.name: SOURCE_LINE_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal identifier of the source line if available.

columns.name: SOURCE_LINE_NUMBER
columns.comments: Represents the user-facing identifier of the source line if available.

columns.name: EXPECTED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the quantity that is expected from the source.

columns.name: UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure code for all quantities being stored in this table.

columns.name: EXPECTED_DATE
columns.comments: Represents the date at which the item is expected to be available.

columns.comments: Identifier of the project used to build the transaction descriptive flexfield for project-related transaction distributions. Foreign key to PJF_PROJECTS_ALL_B.PROJECT_ID.

columns.name: PJC_TASK_ID
columns.comments: Identifier of the task used to build the transaction descriptive flexfield for project-related transaction distributions. Foreign key to PJF_PROJ_ELEMENTS_B.PROJ_ELEMENT_ID (however uses an alias of TASK_ID).

objects.description: This table stores the assignment and shortage information for each material, populated during material assignment.

columns.name: MA_MTL_ASSIGNMENT_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of the material availability assignments record. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal identifier of the work order for which the material is being assigned.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: The organization identifier that represents the manufacturing plant to which the material belongs.

columns.name: WO_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal identifier of the work order operation for which the material is being assigned.

columns.name: INVENTORY_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal identifier of the material that is being assigned.

columns.name: WO_OPERATION_MATERIAL_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal identifier of the work order operation material. This is a foreign key to the WIE_WO_OPERATION_MATERIALS.

columns.name: AVAILABLE_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the total available on-hand quantity for an item.

columns.name: PROJECTED_AVAILABLE_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the quantity available to assign.

columns.name: REQUIRED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Quantity of the material consumed in the operation. This is usually the Work Order Quantity times the QUANTITY_PER_ASSEMBLY when the basis type is VARIABLE.

columns.name: ALLOCATED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: The total allocated quantity for a work order material.

columns.name: PICKED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: The total picked quantity for a work order material.

columns.name: OPEN_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the quantity required for that operation.

columns.name: NET_OPEN_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the total quantity required for that operation.

columns.name: ASSIGNED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the quantity assigned for the material.

columns.name: SHORTAGE_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the shortage if any for the material.

columns.name: EXPECTED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the expected supply if any for the material.

columns.name: RESERVED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: This column represents the total quantity reserved against the work order material.

columns.name: UNRESERVED_ALLOCATED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: This column represents the allocated quantity which does not have corresponding reservations in the INV_RESERVATIONS table.

columns.name: UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure code for all quantities stored in this table.

columns.name: CALCULATION_DATE
columns.comments: Represents the date/time at which the material has been assigned.

columns.name: USE_COMMON_INVENTORY_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag to determine whether material should be issued/returned from common inventory or from the project associated with the work order. A value of Y indicates material should be issued/returned from common inventory. A value of N indicates material should be issued/returned from the project associated with the work order.

columns.name: PJC_PROJECTED_AVAILABLE_QTY
columns.comments: Represents the quantity available to assign from project striped inventory.

columns.name: COMMON_PROJECTED_AVAILABLE_QTY
columns.comments: Represents the quantity available to assign from common inventory.

columns.name: PJC_AVAILABLE_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the available on-hand quantity for an item from project striped inventory.

columns.name: COMMON_AVAILABLE_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the available on-hand quantity for an item from common inventory.

columns.name: PJC_ASSIGNED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the quantity assigned for the material from project striped inventory.

columns.name: COMMON_ASSIGNED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the quantity assigned for the material from common inventory.

columns.name: PJC_EXPECTED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the expected supply for the material when the PROJECT_REFERENCE_ENABLED flag is set to 'Y' for the organization. The value is the sum of project/task supplies associated with the work order and common supplies.

columns.name: SUBSTITUTE_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used indicate whether this component is a substitute or not. Valid values: Y - Substitute N or null - Primary component

columns.name: ENFORCE_INT_REQUIREMENTS
columns.comments: Enforce integer requirement for component's calculated quantity or inverse quantity. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = EGP_SUB_COMP_ENFORCE_INT_REQ. Valid values include: 0 - None - Do not convert to an integer. 1 - Round down - Round it down to the nearest lower integer. 2 - Round up - Round it up to the nearest higher integer.

columns.name: EXTENDED_QUANTITY

objects.name: WIE_OPERATION_TRANSACTIONS
objects.description: This table stores the operation transactions that are recorded for the primary product as the semi finished assembly gets completed and moves from one operation to another. These transactions include operation completion, primary product scrap, primary product reject, as well as, reversal transactions.

columns.name: WO_OPERATION_TRANSACTION_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of an operation transaction record. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: The organization identifier that represents the manufacturing plant to which this operation transaction is performed.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal identifier of the work order. Operation transactions are always performed in the context of a work order.

columns.name: WO_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: The operation from which the primary product quantity is transacted.

columns.name: INVENTORY_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: The primary product identifier defined on the work order. This is an internal column and is de-normalized.

columns.name: FROM_DISPATCH_STATE
columns.comments: The status from which this transaction takes place. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_DISPATCH_STATE.

columns.name: TO_DISPATCH_STATE
columns.comments: The end resulting status where the transaction quantity moves to. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_DISPATCH_STATE.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_TYPE_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the type of operation transaction and will be derived based on the content in FROM_DISPATCH_STATE and TO_DISPATCH_STATE. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_OP_TRANSACTION_TYPE.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_DATE
columns.comments: Date when the operation transaction is performed.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Transactional product quantity that is transacted.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Transactional unit of measure code of the primary product quantity that is transacted.

columns.name: PRIMARY_QUANTITY
columns.comments: This is a calculated field. If the transaction is not done in the primary quantity (Transaction UOM <> Primary UOM) this will have a different value. Onhand is recorded in the primary quantity, hence it is useful to convert and store this against the transaction.

columns.name: PRIMARY_UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure code for the primary quantity. This is denormalized from the item master for ease of driving analytics.

columns.name: REASON_CODE
columns.comments: Reason for either rejecting the quantities at the operation or scrapping at the operation.

columns.name: COMPL_SUBINVENTORY_CODE
columns.comments: Subinventory where the material is drawn from or where the products are completed.

columns.name: COMPL_LOCATOR_ID
columns.comments: The inventory locator where the materials are drawn from or where the products are completed to.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_NOTE
columns.comments: A note that is captured upon performing the operation transaction.

columns.name: PO_HEADER_ID
columns.comments: The Fusion Purchase Order Identifier. The system key.

columns.name: PO_LINE_ID
columns.comments: The Fusion Purchase Order Line Number. The system key identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_SYSTEM_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates the type of source system (i.e. internal or external) from which data is being imported. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_SOURCE_SYSTEM_TYPE.

columns.name: SOURCE_SYSTEM_ID
columns.comments: Represents the identifier of the source system. If the source system type = "INTERNAL" this value equates to the application id. If "EXTERNAL", then it is the source system as defined in the trading community (TCA) source systems table.

columns.name: SOURCE_SYSTEM_CODE
columns.comments: A code used to indicate the source system from which data is being imported. Depending on the source system type, this value could represent an internal Fusion product code or the actual trading community (TCA) source system reference.

columns.name: SOURCE_HEADER_REF
columns.comments: Represents the source system's user-facing header reference identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_HEADER_REF_ID
columns.comments: Represents the source system's internal header reference identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_LINE_REF
columns.comments: Represents the source system's user-facing line reference identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_LINE_REF_ID
columns.comments: Represents the source system's internal line reference identifier.

columns.name: INV_TRANSACTION_ID
columns.comments: Upon successful processing of the completion/return material transaction (the product level transaction associated with the move), we record the successful INV_MATERIAL_TXNS.TRANSACTION_ID back in this column. The INV online API returns this value.

columns.name: INTERFACE_ROW_ID
columns.comments: Represents the operation transactions interface record.

columns.name: INTERFACE_BATCH_ID
columns.comments: Represents the interface batch identifier.

columns.name: WO_OP_TXN_GROUP_ID
columns.comments: A unique identifier used to group multiple operation transactions together. Its primary usage is to support linking electronic records and signatures (ERES) artifacts to one or more operation transactions.

objects.name: WIE_OPERATION_TRANSACTIONS_INT
objects.description: This is the interface table for work order operation transactions. Production progress updates, in terms of partial finished assembly that are completed in an operation, can be interfaced from either third party systems or from contract manufacturers via this interface table. When assembly movements cross over operations that result in automatic material consumption (auto transact materials) or automatic charging of resources, the operation transaction processor writes the appropriate inventory material transaction interface records and WIP resource transaction interface entries and processes them accordingly. Scraps and Rejects are reported at the operation transaction level.

columns.name: INTERFACE_ROW_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of an operation transaction interface record. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: INTERFACE_BATCH_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the user identified code for the interface batch.

columns.name: INTERFACE_BATCH_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal interface batch identifier. This is used to group a batch of interface records for processing. When interface records are brought in via services or the UI, the system will internally generate this value.

columns.name: INTERFACE_STATUS_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the progress of the interface processing with statuses such as ready for processing or currently in process as well as the various flavors of completion statuses. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_INTERFACE_STATUS.

columns.name: TXN_HEADER_NUMBER
columns.comments: This is a user loaded key that uniquely identifies the transaction within the batch. This user key will be used as a handle to connect the child entities (i.e. the WIE_TRANSACTION_LOTS_INT and WIE_TRANSACTION_SERIALS_INT tables) to this parent transaction table.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID

columns.name: INVENTORY_ITEM_ID

columns.name: TO_DISPATCH_STATE

objects.name: WIE_RESOURCE_TRANSACTIONS
objects.description: This table stores the resource transactions that are recorded for the primary product as the semi finished assembly gets completed and moves from one operation to another.

columns.name: WO_RESOURCE_TRANSACTION_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a resource transaction record. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: The organization identifier that represents the manufacturing plant to which this resource transaction is performed.

columns.name: WORK_CENTER_ID
columns.comments: The work center where the resource is charged.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal identifier of the work order. Resource transactions are always performed in the context of a work order.

columns.name: INVENTORY_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: The primary product identifier defined in the work order. This is an internal column and is de-normalized.

columns.name: WO_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: The operation from which the primary product quantity is transacted.

columns.name: OPERATION_SEQ_NUMBER
columns.comments: The operation sequence number. Along with the work order number, will be the unique user key to the work order operation entity.

columns.name: WO_OPERATION_RESOURCE_ID
columns.comments: The operation resource reference from the work order.

columns.name: RESOURCE_SEQ_NUMBER
columns.comments: The resource sequence number. We need this column in a denormalized form here to be able to capture resource transactions which are adhoc in nature and can then result in the creation of a work order operation resource record.

columns.name: RESOURCE_TYPE
columns.comments: Represents the charged resource type. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_RESOURCE_TYPE. De-Normalized for Costing.

columns.name: RESOURCE_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal identifier of the resource.

columns.name: RESOURCE_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the user key for the resource.

columns.name: RESOURCE_ACTIVITY_CODE
columns.comments: Activity is used to define any intra operation steps + any other custom run steps that the customer would like to track at the resource level. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_RESOURCE_ACTIVITY.

columns.name: AUTO_TRANSACT_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag that identifies that this is a system generated transaction.

columns.name: BASIS_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates whether the resource quantity is fixed (i.e. usage per lot produced) or variable (i.e. usage per item produced). Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = EGP_BOM_BASIS_TYPE. De-Normalized for Costing.

columns.name: CHARGE_TYPE
columns.comments: Whether resource transactions were automatically generated and at what stage. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_CHARGE_TYPE. De-Normalized for Costing.

columns.name: USAGE_RATE
columns.comments: The predefined resource rate that is required to perform operation/activity for one unit of the assembly. The usage rate is the value that we will inherit as is from the work definition. For example: Number of hours it take to spray paint one pedestal. De-Normalized for Costing.

columns.name: REQUIRED_USAGE
columns.comments: Represents the required usage for the resource. Based on the basis type it would be the usage per assembly unit [variable] or the usage per work order [fixed]. The planned resource usage is the value applied based on the work order quantity depending on the 'Basis'. For example: Usage rate : 1 hour, Basis : Variable, WO Qty = 10 So, planned resource usage = 1 * 10 = 10 hours. De-Normalized for Costing.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_TYPE_CODE
columns.comments: Identifies the type of the resource transaction. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_TRANSACTION_TYPE.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_DATE
columns.comments: Date when the resource transaction is performed.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the quantity of the resource transaction.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Unit of measure code of the resource quantity that is transacted.

columns.name: PRIMARY_QUANTITY
columns.comments: This is a calculated field. If the transaction is not done in the primary quantity (Transaction UOM <> Primary UOM) this will have a different value. Onhand is recorded in the primary quantity, hence it is useful to convert and store this against the transaction.

columns.name: PRIMARY_UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure code for the primary quantity. This is denormalized from the item master for ease of driving analytics.

columns.name: SOURCE_SYSTEM_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates the type of source system (i.e. internal or external) from which data is being imported. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_SOURCE_SYSTEM_TYPE.

columns.name: SOURCE_SYSTEM_ID
columns.comments: Represents the identifier of the source system. If the source system type = "INTERNAL" this value equates to the application id. If "EXTERNAL", then it is the source system as defined in the trading community (TCA) source systems table.

columns.name: SOURCE_SYSTEM_CODE
columns.comments: A code used to indicate the source system from which data is being imported. Depending on the source system type, this value could represent an internal Fusion product code or the actual trading community (TCA) source system reference.

columns.name: SOURCE_HEADER_REF
columns.comments: Represents the source system's user-facing header reference identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_HEADER_REF_ID
columns.comments: Represents the source system's internal header reference identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_LINE_REF
columns.comments: Represents the source system's user-facing line reference identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_LINE_REF_ID
columns.comments: Represents the source system's internal line reference identifier.

columns.name: WO_OPERATION_TRANSACTION_ID
columns.comments: When the auto-transact flag is checked at the operation level, the operation completion that moves the primary product quantity out of the operation triggers the creation of resource transactions. In such cases, we will have the operation transaction id that triggered this resource transaction.

columns.name: CST_INTERFACED_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag to indicate whether the resource transaction is interfaced to costing or not. The not yet interfaced transaction will become candidates for the ESS job that pushes the transaction to the Fusion Costing system.

objects.name: WIE_RESOURCE_TRANSACTIONS_INT
objects.description: This is the interface table for work order resource transactions. Production progress updates, in terms of resource requirements, are interfaced from either third party systems or from contract manufacturers via this interface table.

columns.name: INTERFACE_ROW_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a resource transaction interface record. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: INTERFACE_BATCH_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the user identified code for the interface batch.

columns.name: INTERFACE_BATCH_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal interface batch identifier. This is used to group a batch of interface records for processing. When interface records are brought in via services or the UI, the system will internally generate this value.

columns.name: INTERFACE_STATUS_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the progress of the interface processing with statuses such as ready for processing or currently in process as well as the various flavors of completion statuses. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_INTERFACE_STATUS.

columns.name: TXN_HEADER_NUMBER
columns.comments: This is a user loaded key that uniquely identifies the transaction within the batch. This user key will be used as a handle to connect the child entities (i.e. the WIE_TRANSACTION_LOTS_INT and WIE_TRANSACTION_SERIALS_INT tables) to this parent transaction table.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_CODE
columns.comments: The organization code that represents the manufacturing plant to which this resource transaction is performed.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: The organization identifier that represents the manufacturing plant to which this resource transaction is performed.

columns.name: WORK_CENTER_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the user-key for the work center to which this resource is charged.

columns.name: WORK_CENTER_ID
columns.comments: The identifier of the work center to which this resource is charged.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_NUMBER
columns.comments: Represents the user-facing identifier of the work order. Resource transactions are always performed in the context of a work order.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal identifier of the work order. Resource transactions are always performed in the context of a work order.

columns.name: WO_OPERATION_SEQ_NUMBER
columns.comments: Represents the work order operation sequence from which this resource transaction is being performed.

columns.name: WO_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: The internal identifier of the operation from which the resource quantity is transacted.

columns.name: WO_RESOURCE_SEQ_NUMBER
columns.comments: Represents the sequence number of the resource associated to this work order operation resource transaction.

columns.name: WO_OPERATION_RESOURCE_ID
columns.comments: Represents the work order operation resource for the resource being transacted.

columns.name: RESOURCE_CODE
columns.comments: The user key for the resource against which the quantity is transacted.

columns.name: RESOURCE_ID
columns.comments: The internal identifier of the resource against which the quantity is transacted.

columns.name: RESOURCE_ACTIVITY_CODE
columns.comments: Indicates the activity this production resource is performing at this operation. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_RESOURCE_ACTIVITY.

columns.name: BASIS_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates whether the resource quantity is fixed (i.e. usage per lot produced) or variable (i.e. usage per item produced). Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = EGP_BOM_BASIS_TYPE.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_TYPE_CODE
columns.comments: Identifies the type of the resource transaction. Valid values are listed in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_TRANSACTION_TYPES.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_DATE
columns.comments: Date when the resource transaction is performed.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Resource quantity that is being transacted.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure code of the resource quantity being transacted.

columns.name: TRANSACTION_UNIT_OF_MEASURE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure of the resource quantity being transacted.

columns.name: SOURCE_SYSTEM_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates the type of source system (i.e. internal or external) from which data is being imported. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_SOURCE_SYSTEM_TYPE.

columns.name: SOURCE_SYSTEM_CODE
columns.comments: A code used to indicate the source system from which data is being imported. Depending on the source system type, this value could represent an internal Fusion product code or the actual trading community (TCA) source system reference.

columns.name: SOURCE_SYSTEM_ID
columns.comments: Represents the identifier of the source system. If the source system type = "INTERNAL" this value equates to the application id. If "EXTERNAL", then it is the source system as defined in the trading community (TCA) source systems table.

columns.name: SOURCE_HEADER_REF
columns.comments: Represents the source system's user-facing header reference identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_HEADER_REF_ID
columns.comments: Represents the source system's internal header reference identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_LINE_REF
columns.comments: Represents the source system's user-facing line reference identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_LINE_REF_ID
columns.comments: Represents the source system's internal line reference identifier.

columns.comments: This is an internal column that is used to link backflush resource transaction interface records to an associated operation transaction interface record.

columns.name: WO_RESOURCE_TRANSACTION_ID

columns.name: WO_SERIAL_TRANSACTION_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a transaction serials record. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: WO_TRANSACTION_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal identifier of the operation transaction. This is a foreign key to the WIE_OPERATION_TRANSACTIONS table. For serialized manufacturing, from the operation that begins the serialization, serial numbers are required in the transacted operation. Also used in the product level inventory transaction in the context of operation for non serialized manufacturing cases where the end assembly product is serial controlled.

columns.name: WO_LOT_TRANSACTION_ID
columns.comments: When the item is lot and serial controlled, the serials that are transacted in the lots are connected by a foreign key reference to the WIE_TRANSACTION_LOTS table.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID

columns.name: INVENTORY_ITEM_ID

columns.comments: Lot number. This column is populated for lot and serial controlled items.

columns.name: SERIAL_NUMBER

columns.name: PARENT_SERIAL_NUMBER
columns.comments: The serial number of the parent product. When component serials are transacted(issues), users can optionally specify which parent serial these specific component serial goes in to. For serialization enabled jobs, these can happen when auto transactions are triggers as assembly serials are completed at operations.

objects.name: WIE_WORK_ORDERS_B
objects.description: This table stores information about what it takes to make a product. It identifies the primary product and can optionally refer to the Item Structure used to define material requirements. Work Definition also specifies the sequence of operation steps and the related resources that are necessary to manufacture the product. Work Definition serves different purposes. It is used to calculate standard costs of the manufactured product(s). It is also used by planning/scheduling and serves as a template to create standard work orders

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of work order record. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: The organization identifier that represents the manufacturing plant to which this work order belongs.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_NUMBER
columns.comments: Represents the user-facing identifier of the work order.

columns.name: WORK_METHOD_ID
columns.comments: Represents the work method identifier for this work order. The work method indicates the type of work being executed within the Fusion Manufacturing application.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates the type of this work order. Values are contained within the ORA_WIE_WO_TYPE lookup if this work order is a manufacturing work order. If this is a maintenance work order, valid values are contained within the ORA_MNT_WO_TYPE lookup.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_SUB_TYPE
columns.comments: The subtype specifically will be populated for non-standard work. This is used to derive the appropriate costing account for non-standard work. Values are contained in the ORA_WIE_WO_SUB_TYPE lookup if this work order is a manufacturing work order. If this is a maintenance work order, valid values are contained within the ORA_MNT_WO_SUB_TYPE lookup.

columns.name: INVENTORY_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: Refers to the top level, final assembly, subassembly, or model item which belongs to the given organization.

columns.name: ITEM_REVISION
columns.comments: If the primary product is revision controlled, this will have a value.

columns.name: ITEM_VERSION
columns.comments: If the item is version controlled, this value will be populated. At the time of work order creation, the work definition selection API returns the valid item version based on the work definition as of date. And that value will be persisted here.

columns.name: ITEM_STRUCTURE_NAME
columns.comments: Item Structure Name (aka alternate_bom_designator). This is how it used to be called in EBS. In Fusion PIM it is called as Item Structure Name. This will be populated programmatically and will not be captured by the end user.

columns.name: TRANSFORM_FROM_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: Refers to the assembly item that is being transformed to a new assembly item on a Transform work order.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_AS_OF_DATE
columns.comments: The As-Of-Date is used to figure out the proper version of the work definition when the Org + Product + As-Of-Date is provided as the filter criteria in narrowing down the work order.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_ID
columns.comments: The foreign key reference to the work definition.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_VERSION_ID
columns.comments: The version of the work definition.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_PRIORITY
columns.comments: Used to set the priority of the work order depending on the demand that needed to be prioritized.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_STATUS_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal identifier of the user-defined status of the work order.

columns.name: SCHEDULING_METHOD
columns.comments: The scheduling method indicates if the work order is scheduled or not. A value of 'NO_SCHEDULING' indicates the work order is not scheduled. A value of 'DEFAULT_SCHEDULER' indicates the work order will be scheduled using the default infinite scheduler. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_WO_SCHEDULING_METHOD.

columns.name: PLANNED_START_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Refers to the planned work order quantity which should be greater than zero for standard work orders, and can be equal to or greater than zero for non standard work orders.

columns.name: NETTABLE_SUPPLY_QTY_OVERRIDE
columns.comments: This is a user entered override of the completion quantity intended to indicate if there are work order specific variances compared to the calculated Completion Quantity

columns.name: UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure code. The assembly quantity will be produced in this UOM. The transactions that moves the assembly from operation to operation and also eventually the completions will be performed in this UOM.

columns.name: PRIMARY_PRODUCT_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the output quantity of the primary product used to create the work order.

columns.name: PRIMARY_PRODUCT_UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure code of the primary product used to create the work order.

columns.name: FIRM_PLANNED_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag to allow or prevent Planning from suggesting rescheduling and re-planning recommendations with respect to the Work Order. When the flag is on, this work order will not be considered by MRP to reschedule or re-plan.

columns.name: PLANNED_START_DATE
columns.comments: Planned start date of the work order.

columns.name: PLANNED_COMPLETION_DATE
columns.comments: Planned completion date of the work order.

columns.name: ACTUAL_START_DATE
columns.comments: Actual start date of the work order.

columns.name: ACTUAL_COMPLETION_DATE
columns.comments: Actual completion date of the work order.

columns.name: RELEASED_DATE
columns.comments: Date when the work order is released.

columns.name: CLOSED_DATE
columns.comments: Date when the work order is closed.

columns.name: CANCELED_DATE
columns.comments: Date when the work order is canceled.

columns.name: CANCELED_REASON
columns.comments: Reason for which the work order is canceled. This is a free format text.

columns.name: NEED_BY_DATE
columns.comments: Date when the supply created by the work order will be used to fulfill a demand.

columns.name: STATUS_CHANGE_REASON
columns.comments: The reason which is a free format capture of why the status is changed. The most current status change reason will be persisted in this column.

columns.name: COMPLETED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Primary product quantity completed so far in the work order. This is a summary column.

columns.name: SCRAPPED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Primary product quantity that is scrapped in the work order. This is a summary column.

columns.name: REJECTED_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Primary product quantity that is rejected in the work order. This is a summary column.

columns.name: OVERCOMPL_TOLERANCE_TYPE
columns.comments: The tolerance type for over completions. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = EGP_OVER_TOLTYPE.

columns.name: OVERCOMPL_TOLERANCE_VALUE
columns.comments: The percent or amount value that is allowed over the scheduled completion work order quantity.

columns.name: UNDERCOMPL_TOLERANCE_TYPE
columns.comments: The tolerance type for under completions. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_EGP_UNDER_COMP_TOL.

columns.name: UNDERCOMPL_TOLERANCE_VALUE
columns.comments: The percent or amount value that is allowed under the scheduled completion work order quantity.

columns.name: UNDER_COMPLETED_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag to indicate that the work order is marked as under-completed.

columns.name: SUPPLY_TYPE
columns.comments: The various supply types are "Assembly Pull", "Operation Pull", "Push", and "Phantom". Assembly Pull - Material will be backflushed at the completion of the assembly. Operation Pull - Material will be backflushed at the completion of the operation. Push - Material will have to manually issued. Phantom - For materials having lower level components, the components will be considered as inputs to this work order. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup_type = EGP_WIP_SUP_TYPE + lookup_type = ORA_WIE_WO_SUPPLY_TYPE.

columns.name: COMPL_SUBINVENTORY_CODE
columns.comments: The default completion subinventory for the primary product.

columns.name: COMPL_LOCATOR_ID
columns.comments: The default completion locator for the primary product, if the subinventory is locator controlled.

columns.name: SERIAL_TRACKING_FLAG
columns.comments: Indicates that the end item (eg assembly in discrete manufacturing) is tracked by serial numbers during work execution. The partially finished assembly starts its serialization during the lifecycle of the work order. This again depends on the serial control policies of the primary product and the enablement of the serialization at a particular operation within the work order.

columns.name: BACK_TO_BACK_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag to indicate that the work order is created as a result of a back-to-back flow.

columns.name: ORCHESTRATION_CODE
columns.comments: Attribute made available for integrating stakeholders to retain and persist a handle in the work orders schema to filter out events that make only sense to them. Stakeholders include SCO and Planning.

columns.name: INTERFACE_SOURCE_CODE
columns.comments: Attribute made available for integrating stakeholders to retain and persist a handle in the work orders schema to filter out events that make only sense to them. Stakeholders include SCO and Planning.

columns.name: SCO_SUPPLY_ORDER_ID
columns.comments: When Supply Chain Orchestration (SCO) creates the Work Order, this column contains an order reference populated by the SCO process. For manually created CM orders, or when Planning creates the CM Order in Manufacturing directly, this reference is not populated. SCO then reads these SCO unaware CM work orders via an ESS program and creates them in the SCO repository.

columns.name: CONTRACT_MFG_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag to indicate that the work order is a contract manufacturing work order.

columns.name: CM_PO_HEADER_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal identifier of the contract manufacturer's purchase order.

columns.name: CM_PO_LINE_ID
columns.comments: The reference to the contract manufacturer's PO line identifier. In R11, The PO line will have the item that is identified as a CM Service Item (or also called as the CM FG Server in the examples) in the PO line. It is not the primary product on the work order.

columns.name: CM_PO_LINE_LOC_ID
columns.comments: The reference to the contract manufacturer's PO schedule line reference. This will be populated only when the WO is created in the contract manufacturing organization.

columns.name: ORDER_LESS_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag to indicate if the work order represents an 'orderless' order.

columns.name: SOURCE_SYSTEM_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates the type of source system (i.e. internal or external) from which data is being imported. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_SOURCE_SYSTEM_TYPE.

columns.name: SOURCE_SYSTEM_ID
columns.comments: Represents the identifier of the source system. If the source system type = "INTERNAL" this value equates to the application id. If "EXTERNAL", then it is the source system as defined in the trading community (TCA) source systems table.

columns.name: SOURCE_HEADER_REF
columns.comments: Represents the source system's user-facing header reference identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_HEADER_REF_ID
columns.comments: Represents the source system's internal header reference identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_LINE_REF
columns.comments: Represents the source system's user-facing line reference identifier.

columns.name: SOURCE_LINE_REF_ID
columns.comments: Represents the source system's internal line reference identifier.

columns.name: MNT_FORECAST_ID
columns.comments: Reference to the maintenance forecast that created the work order. Foreign key to MNT_FORECASTS.FORECAST_ID.

columns.name: PJC_CONTEXT_CATEGORY
columns.comments: Segment used to identify the descriptive flexfield application context for project-related standardized cost collection.

columns.name: PJC_PROJECT_ID
columns.comments: Identifier of the project used to build the transaction descriptive flexfield for project-related transaction distributions. Foreign key to PJF_PROJECTS_ALL_B.PROJECT_ID.

columns.name: PJC_PROJECT_NUMBER
columns.comments: The number assigned to a project.

columns.name: PJC_TASK_ID

columns.name: PJC_TASK_NUMBER
columns.comments: The identifying number for a task which is a subdivision of project work.

columns.name: PJC_EXPENDITURE_TYPE_ID
columns.comments: Expenditure type used to build the transaction descriptive flexfield for project-related transaction distributions.

columns.name: PJC_EXPENDITURE_ITEM_DATE
columns.comments: Date on which a project-related transaction is incurred.

columns.name: PJC_ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: Identifier for expenditure organization used to build the transaction descriptive flexfield for project-related transaction distributions.

columns.name: PJC_BILLABLE_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag that indicates if a project-related item is available to be billed to customers. Valid values are Y or N.

columns.name: PJC_CAPITALIZABLE_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag that indicates if a project-related item is eligible for capitalization. Valid values are Y or N.

columns.name: PJC_WORK_TYPE_ID
columns.comments: Identifier for project-related classification of the worked performed.

columns.comments: Identifier of contract. This attribute is used when Oracle Contract Billing or Oracle Grants Accounting is installed.

columns.name: PJC_CONTRACT_LINE_ID
columns.comments: Tracks contract line information. This attribute is used when Oracle Contract Billing or Oracle Grants Accounting is installed.

columns.name: PJC_FUNDING_ALLOCATION_ID
columns.comments: Specifies the name of the project funding override. This attribute is used when Oracle Contract Billing or Oracle Grants Accounting is installed.
