columns.name: CODE
columns.comments: The unique user key to the respective setup business object.

columns.name: NAME
columns.comments: The alternate translatable key to the respective setup business object.

columns.name: DESCRIPTION
columns.comments: The description of the respective setup business object entity.

columns.name: SEEDED_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate whether the setup business object record is seeded or not. Default is 'Y'.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: SEED_DATA_SOURCE
columns.comments: Source of seed data record. A value of 'BULK_SEED_DATA_SCRIPT' indicates that record was bulk loaded. Otherwise, specifies the name of the seed data file.

columns.name: ORA_SEED_SET1
columns.comments: Oracle internal use only. Indicates the edition-based redefinition (EBR) context of the row for SET1. Context values are Y or N.

columns.name: ORA_SEED_SET2
columns.comments: Oracle internal use only. Indicates the edition-based redefinition (EBR) context of the row for SET2. Context values are Y or N.

objects.name: WIS_STANDARD_OPERATIONS_B
objects.description: This table stores the plant specific standard operation definition. A standard operation is a reusable definition of the process step used in the manufacturing process. This includes all the resource requirements and material requirements to carry out the process step. Examples are: 'etch the company logo' and 'drill a three inch hole'.

columns.name: STANDARD_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a standard operation. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: STANDARD_OPERATION_CODE
columns.comments: A code that represents the user key to the standard operation.

columns.name: OPERATION_TYPE
columns.comments: Specifies the type of the operation. Valid values are contained within the ORA_WIS_OPERATION_TYPE lookup.

columns.name: COUNT_POINT_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate if this is a count point operation. If an operation is a count point operation, then you have to manually complete it. Any operations in between the count points are automatically completed (i.e. backflushed, etc.).

columns.name: AUTO_TRANSACT_FLAG
columns.comments: Indicates whether both resources and materials are automatically charged based on the supply type or the charge type setups for the operation. If the supply type is Operation Pull, the component level issue transactions will happen when the operation is completed. If the supply type is Assembly Pull, the component level issue transactions will happen at the assembly completion event. Resource transactions are automatically done when the quantity is moved outside the operation. Valid values are 'Y' and 'N'.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: The organization identifier that represents the manufacturing plant to which this standard operation belongs.

columns.name: WORK_CENTER_ID
columns.comments: Indicates the work center where this operation is executed.

columns.name: INACTIVE_DATE
columns.comments: The date on which this standard operation has become inactive. If no date is specified, the standard operation is considered active.

columns.name: USED_IN_AUTO_WD_FLAG
columns.comments: Indicates that this standard operation is to be used as the default operation when creating an automated work definition. Only one standard operation is allowed to have this column set to a 'Y'. Valid Values: 'Y' and 'N'.

columns.name: OSP_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: Item that represents the value added service in a supplier operation. This is also commonly known as a partially finished assembly.

columns.name: SUPPLIER_ID
columns.comments: Represents the identifier of the suggested supplier for a supplier operation.

columns.name: SUPPLIER_SITE_ID
columns.comments: Represents the identifier of the suggested supplier site for a supplier operation.

columns.name: LEAD_TIME_UOM
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure for the fixed and/or variable lead time values on the supplier operation.

columns.name: FIXED_LEAD_TIME
columns.comments: Represents the fixed lead time used to calculate the operation's start and end date for the supplier operation.

columns.name: VARIABLE_LEAD_TIME
columns.comments: Represents the variable lead time used to calculate the operation's start and end date based on the operation quantity for the supplier operation.

columns.name: ADDL_MTL_AT_MANUAL_ISSUE
columns.comments: Indicates whether or not this operation allows additional materials to be added at manual issue. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_ADDL_MANUAL_ISSUE_OPTS.

columns.name: OP_COMPL_WITH_UNDER_ISSUE
columns.comments: Indicates whether or not to allow operation completions with under issued material. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_OP_COMPLETION_VAL_OPTS.

columns.name: OP_COMPL_WITH_OPEN_EXCEPTIONS
columns.comments: Indicates whether or not to allow operation completions with open exceptions. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_OP_COMPLETION_VAL_OPTS.

columns.name: REASON_FOR_REPAIR_CODE_ID
columns.comments: Represents the primary reason for which this operation is performed. Foreign key to cse_condition_event_codes_b table.

columns.name: REPAIR_TXN_CODE_ID
columns.comments: Represents the default codified transaction for which the material and resource consumed in the operation should be associated to. Foreign key to cse_condition_event_codes_b table.

columns.name: WORK_ACCOMPLISHED_CODE_ID
columns.comments: Represents the default accomplishment code to record when the operation is completed. Foreign key to cse_condition_event_codes_b table.

columns.name: OP_YIELD_FACTOR
columns.comments: Indicates the yield factor which represents the percentage of the starting quantity that is actually yielded at the completion of the operation. The default value is 1 (100%).

columns.name: COMMON_STANDARD_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: Reference to the unique identifier of the global standard operation created in the master organization.

columns.name: LAST_SYNC_DATE
columns.comments: Represents the date/time this record was last synchronized with the referenced standard operations.

columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: STD_OPERATION_RESOURCE_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a standard operation resource. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: RESOURCE_SEQ_NUMBER
columns.comments: Defines the actual sequence of the resource used in the operation. Multiple resources can be scheduled to be working concurrently within the same operation. Simultaneity is implemented by having more than one resource with the same sequence number.

columns.name: ASSIGNED_UNITS
columns.comments: Indicates the number of resource instances assigned to this operation.

columns.name: USAGE_RATE
columns.comments: The resource usage rate to yield one unit of product.

columns.name: UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure code of the resource usage rate.

columns.name: BASIS_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates whether the resource usage is fixed (i.e. usage per lot produced) or variable (i.e. usage per item produced). Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = EGP_BOM_BASIS_TYPE.

columns.name: SCHEDULE_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates if this resource is scheduled or not. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_RESOURCE_SCHEDULE.

columns.name: PRINCIPAL_FLAG
columns.comments: When two or more resources are running in parallel (i.e. simultaneous resources which have the same sequence number), one and only one of them must be marked as the principal/primary resource. Planning will identify bottlenecks if the principal resource is not available when checking for capacity.

columns.name: CHARGE_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates how the resource is charged during work execution. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_CHARGE_TYPE.

columns.name: RESOURCE_ACTIVITY_CODE
columns.comments: Indicates the activity this production resource is going to perform at this operation. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_RESOURCE_ACTIVITY.

columns.name: INVERSE_USAGE_RATE
columns.comments: Indicates the inverse resource usage rate.

columns.name: STANDARD_OPERATION_ID

columns.name: WORK_CENTER_ID

objects.name: WIS_WC_RESOURCE_SHIFT_EXCPS

columns.name: RESOURCE_SHIFT_EXCEPTION_ID

columns.comments: Identifies the type of resource exception.

columns.comments: Indicates the number of resource instances to increase or decrease.

columns.comments: For Add Capacity or Reduce Capacity, it is the date when capacity change ends.

columns.name: FROM_TIME
columns.comments: Required only for Add Capacity or Reduce Capacity. It is the time associated with the From Date

columns.name: TO_TIME
columns.comments: Required only for Add Capacity or Reduce Capacity. It is the time associated with the From Date.

columns.name: REASON_CODE
columns.comments: Indicates the reason for the resource shift exception.

columns.comments: This indicates the resource to which this shift exception is defined.

objects.name: WIS_WD_CONDITIONS
objects.description: This table stores the details of a condition. A condition is a combination of one parameter, one condition and one value (i.e. 'PH >7').

columns.name: WD_CONDITION_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a work definition condition. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: CONDITION_OPERATOR
columns.comments: Indicates the operator of the condition.

columns.name: ATTRIBUTE_TYPE
columns.comments: Determine the type of attribute this condition is based on. Valid values include: - ITEM (option item) - TIA (transaction item attribute) - UDA (user defined attribute)

columns.name: ATTRIBUTE_VALUE
columns.comments: This is the value of the attribute for which the condition applies.

columns.name: ATTRIBUTE_PK1_VALUE
columns.comments: Indicate the part 1 primary key value of the attribute.

columns.name: ATTRIBUTE_PK2_VALUE
columns.comments: Indicate the part 2 primary key value of the attribute.

columns.name: ATTRIBUTE_PK3_VALUE
columns.comments: Indicate the part 3 primary key value of the attribute.

columns.name: OBJECT_NAME
columns.comments: Name of the object to which the condition applies.

columns.name: OBJECT_PK_VALUE
columns.comments: Primary key value of the object for which this condition applies.

columns.name: WD_CONDITION_GROUP_ID
columns.comments: Indicates the condition group this condition belongs to.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

objects.name: WIS_WD_CONDITION_GROUPS

columns.name: WD_CONDITION_GROUP_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a work definition condition group. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER

columns.name: CONDITION_GROUP_OPERATOR

columns.name: NESTED_CONDITION_FLAG

columns.name: OBJECT_NAME

columns.name: OBJECT_PK_VALUE

columns.name: PARENT_CONDITION_GROUP_ID
columns.comments: Indicates the parent condition group internal identifier.

objects.name: WIS_WD_DETAILS_INT
objects.description: This is the interface table for work definition details.

columns.name: INTERFACE_ROW_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a work definition interface record. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: INTERFACE_BATCH_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the user identified code for the interface batch.

columns.name: INTERFACE_BATCH_ID
columns.comments: Represents the internal interface batch identifier. This is used to group a batch of interface records for processing. When interface records are brought in via services or the UI, the system will internally generate this value.

columns.name: INTERFACE_STATUS_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the progress of the interface processing with statuses such as ready for processing or currently in process as well as the various flavors of completion statuses. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIE_INTERFACE_STATUS.

columns.name: HEADER_NUMBER
columns.comments: This attribute allows the user to connect the header records with the details in the various work definition interface details tables.

columns.name: ACTION_CODE
columns.comments: A code used to indicate if the system should create or update this entity. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_WD_IMP_DETAIL_ACTION.

columns.name: LOAD_TYPE
columns.comments: A code used to indicate the type of data this detail record contains. This indicates if the data being loaded represents the work definition operation, work definition operation material, work definition operation resource, etc. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_WD_IMP_LOAD_TYPE.

columns.name: HEADER_INT_ROW_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of the row in the header interface table associated with this detail record.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: The organization identifier that represents the manufacturing plant to which this work definition operation belongs.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_ID
columns.comments: Represents the work definition identifier that is the foreign key to the WIS_WORK_DEFINITIONS table.

columns.name: OPERATION_NAME
columns.comments: Indicates the name of the work definition operation.

columns.name: OPERATION_DESCRIPTION
columns.comments: Indicates the description of the work definition operation.

columns.name: OPERATION_LONG_DESCRIPTION
columns.comments: Indicates the long description of the work definition operation.

columns.name: OPERATION_TYPE
columns.comments: Specifies the type of the operation. Valid values are contained within the ORA_WIS_OPERATION_TYPE lookup.

columns.name: OPERATION_SEQ_NUMBER
columns.comments: Indicates the execution sequence of the operation.

columns.name: WD_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a work definition operation. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: EFFECTIVE_FROM_DATE
columns.comments: Indicates the date from which this operation is effective.

columns.name: EFFECTIVE_TO_DATE
columns.comments: Indicates the date from which this operation is no longer effective.

columns.name: WORK_CENTER_CODE
columns.comments: Indicates the user key of the work center where this operation is executed.

columns.name: WORK_CENTER_ID
columns.comments: Indicates the work center where this operation is executed.

columns.name: COUNT_POINT_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate if this is a count point operation. If an operation is a count point operation, then you have to manually complete it. Any operations in between the count points are automatically completed (i.e. backflushed, etc.).

columns.name: AUTO_TRANSACT_FLAG
columns.comments: Indicates whether both resources and materials are automatically charged based on the supply type or the charge type setups for the operation. If the supply type is Operation Pull, the component level issue transactions will happen when the operation is completed. If the supply type is Assembly Pull, the component level issue transactions will happen at the assembly completion event. Resource transactions are automatically done when the quantity is moved outside the operation. Valid values are 'Y' and 'N'.

columns.name: SERIAL_TRACKING_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate that the product is tracked by serial number while executing this operation.

columns.name: OPTION_DEPENDENT_FLAG
columns.comments: Indicates whether the operation is dependent on the choice of one or multiple optional components. This applies to an ATO Model work definition only.

columns.name: PLANNING_PERCENT
columns.comments: Percentage used by planning for resources forecast explosion. This applies to an ATO Model work definition only.

columns.name: RULE_TEXT
columns.comments: Holds the text which represents the rule in the format entered by the user.

columns.name: APPLICABILITY_RULE_ID
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate whether the operation is dependent on the choice of one or multiple optional components. This applies to an ATO Model work definition only.

columns.name: ADDL_MTL_AT_MANUAL_ISSUE
columns.comments: Indicates whether or not this operation allows additional materials to be added at manual issue. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_ADDL_MANUAL_ISSUE_OPTS.

columns.name: OP_COMPL_WITH_UNDER_ISSUE
columns.comments: Indicates whether or not to allow operation completions with under issued material. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_OP_COMPLETION_VAL_OPTS.

columns.name: OP_COMPL_WITH_OPEN_EXCEPTIONS
columns.comments: Indicates whether or not to allow operation completions with open exceptions. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_OP_COMPLETION_VAL_OPTS.

columns.name: REFERENCED_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate whether this operation references a standard operation.

columns.name: STANDARD_OPERATION_CODE
columns.comments: A code that represents the user key to the standard operation.

columns.name: STANDARD_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: Represents the standard operation identifier that is the foreign key to the WIS_STANDARD_OPERATIONS_B table.

columns.name: SHIPPING_DOCUMENTS_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to determine whether shipping documents need to be generated for a supplier operation. Valid Values: 'Y' and 'N'.

columns.name: OSP_ITEM_NUMBER
columns.comments: Item number that represents the value added service in a supplier operation. This is also commonly known as a partially finished assembly.

columns.name: OSP_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: Item identifier that represents the value added service in a supplier operation. This is also commonly known as a partially finished assembly.

columns.name: SUPPLIER_NAME
columns.comments: Represents the name of the suggested supplier for a supplier operation.

columns.name: SUPPLIER_ID
columns.comments: Represents the identifier of the suggested supplier for a supplier operation.

columns.name: SUPPLIER_SITE_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the code of the suggested supplier site for a supplier operation.

columns.name: SUPPLIER_SITE_ID
columns.comments: Represents the identifier of the suggested supplier site for a supplier operation.

columns.name: LEAD_TIME_UOM
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure code for the fixed and/or variable lead time values on the supplier operation.

columns.name: LEAD_TIME_UNIT_OF_MEASURE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure for the fixed and/or variable lead time values on the supplier operation.

columns.name: FIXED_LEAD_TIME
columns.comments: Represents the fixed lead time used to calculate the operation's start and end date for the supplier operation.

columns.name: VARIABLE_LEAD_TIME
columns.comments: Represents the variable lead time used to calculate the operation's start and end date based on the operation quantity for the supplier operation.

columns.name: LEAD_TIME_PERCENT
columns.comments: Represents the offset percent used in lead time roll up to calculate the cumulative lead times.

columns.name: WORKER_ID
columns.comments: The partition number for multi-threading.

columns.name: RESOURCE_SEQ_NUMBER
columns.comments: Defines the actual sequence of the resource used in the operation. Multiple resources can be scheduled to be working concurrently within the same operation. Simultaneity is implemented by having more than one resource with the same sequence number.

columns.name: WD_OPERATION_RESOURCE_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a work definition operation resource. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: ASSIGNED_UNITS

columns.name: USAGE_RATE

columns.name: UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure code of the resource usage rate.

columns.name: BASIS_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates whether the resource usage is fixed (i.e. usage per lot produced) or variable (i.e. usage per item produced). Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = EGP_BOM_BASIS_TYPE.

columns.name: SCHEDULE_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates if this resource is scheduled or not. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_RESOURCE_SCHEDULE.

columns.name: PRINCIPAL_FLAG
columns.comments: When two or more resources are running in parallel (i.e. simultaneous resources which have the same sequence number), one and only one of them must be marked as the principal/primary resource. Planning will identify bottlenecks if the principal resource is not available when checking for capacity.

columns.name: CHARGE_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates how the resource is charged during work execution. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_CHARGE_TYPE.

columns.name: RESOURCE_ACTIVITY_CODE

objects.name: WIS_WD_OPERATIONS_B
objects.description: This table is used to define the list of sequenced operations that are necessary to manufacture the specified product.

columns.name: WD_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a work definition operation. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_ID
columns.comments: Represents the work definition identifier that is the foreign key to the WIS_WORK_DEFINITIONS table.

columns.name: OPERATION_TYPE
columns.comments: Specifies the type of the operation. Valid values are contained within the ORA_WIS_OPERATION_TYPE lookup.

columns.name: OPERATION_SEQ_NUMBER
columns.comments: Indicates the execution sequence of the operation.

columns.name: WORK_CENTER_ID
columns.comments: Indicates the work center where this operation is executed.

columns.name: EFFECTIVE_FROM_DATE
columns.comments: Indicates the date from which this operation is effective.

columns.name: EFFECTIVE_TO_DATE
columns.comments: Indicates the date from which this operation is no longer effective.

columns.name: COUNT_POINT_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate if this is a count point operation. If an operation is a count point operation, then you have to manually complete it. Any operations in between the count points are automatically completed (i.e. backflushed, etc.).

columns.name: AUTO_TRANSACT_FLAG
columns.comments: Indicates whether both resources and materials are automatically charged based on the supply type or the charge type setups for the operation. If the supply type is Operation Pull, the component level issue transactions will happen when the operation is completed. If the supply type is Assembly Pull, the component level issue transactions will happen at the assembly completion event. Resource transactions are automatically done when the quantity is moved outside the operation. Valid values are 'Y' and 'N'.

columns.name: SERIAL_TRACKING_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate that the product is tracked by serial number while executing this operation.

columns.name: APPLICABILITY_RULE_ID
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate whether the operation is dependent on the choice of one or multiple optional components. This applies to an ATO Model work definition only.

columns.name: OPTION_DEPENDENT_FLAG
columns.comments: Indicates whether the operation is dependent on the choice of one or multiple optional components. This applies to an ATO Model work definition only.

columns.name: PLANNING_PERCENT
columns.comments: Percentage used by planning for resources forecast explosion. This applies to an ATO Model work definition only.

columns.name: REFERENCED_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate whether this operation references a standard operation.

columns.name: STANDARD_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: Represents the standard operation identifier that is the foreign key to the WIS_STANDARD_OPERATIONS_B table.

columns.name: SHIPPING_DOCUMENTS_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to determine whether shipping documents need to be generated for a supplier operation. Valid Values: 'Y' and 'N'.

columns.name: OSP_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: Item that represents the value added service in a supplier operation. This is also commonly known as a partially finished assembly.

columns.name: SUPPLIER_ID
columns.comments: Represents the identifier of the suggested supplier for a supplier operation.

columns.name: SUPPLIER_SITE_ID
columns.comments: Represents the identifier of the suggested supplier site for a supplier operation.

columns.name: LEAD_TIME_UOM
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure for the fixed and/or variable lead time values on the supplier operation.

columns.name: FIXED_LEAD_TIME
columns.comments: Represents the fixed lead time used to calculate the operation's start and end date for the supplier operation.

columns.name: VARIABLE_LEAD_TIME
columns.comments: Represents the variable lead time used to calculate the operation's start and end date based on the operation quantity for the supplier operation.

columns.name: LEAD_TIME_PERCENT
columns.comments: Represents the offset percent used in lead time roll up to calculate the cumulative lead times.

columns.name: ACTION_STATUS_CODE
columns.comments: A code used to represent the last action performed on the work definition operation which caused it to trigger the approvals workflow. Valid values are CREATE and DELETE. An empty/null value indicates this record has been reviewed and approved.

columns.name: ADDL_MTL_AT_MANUAL_ISSUE
columns.comments: Indicates whether or not this operation allows additional materials to be added at manual issue. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_ADDL_MANUAL_ISSUE_OPTS.

columns.name: OP_COMPL_WITH_UNDER_ISSUE
columns.comments: Indicates whether or not to allow operation completions with under issued material. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_OP_COMPLETION_VAL_OPTS.

columns.name: OP_COMPL_WITH_OPEN_EXCEPTIONS
columns.comments: Indicates whether or not to allow operation completions with open exceptions. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_OP_COMPLETION_VAL_OPTS.

columns.name: RESEQUENCE_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate if the operation can be re-sequenced while executing the operation. Valid values are Y or N.

columns.name: OP_YIELD_FACTOR
columns.comments: Indicates the yield factor which represents the percentage of the starting quantity that is actually yielded at the completion of the operation. The default value is 1 (100%).

columns.name: LINE_OP_SEQ_NUMBER
columns.comments: Indicates the production line operation sequence number.

columns.name: WORK_INSTRUCTION_REQUIRED_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate if a operation has a mandatory work instruction.

columns.name: ENFORCE_INSTRUCTIONS
columns.comments: Indicates whether the instructions associated with the operation are optional, required once, or required at every completion. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_INSTRUCTIONS_ENFORCE.

columns.name: CHANGE_LINE_ID
columns.comments: A unique identifier of a change order line. This is the change order line for the work definition to which the operation belongs. This is a foreign key to change_line_id of ego_change_lines_b.

columns.name: IMPLEMENTATION_DATE
columns.comments: Represents the date on which the change order line is scheduled to be implemented.

columns.name: CHANGE_BIT_MAP
columns.comments: Attribute indicating attribute changed value. Default value is 0.

columns.name: ACD_TYPE
columns.comments: Attribute indicating change affected by change order. Valid values are ADD/DELETE/UPDATE/COPY.

columns.name: OLD_WD_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: Identifier of the original work definition operation row the change order affects.

columns.name: WORKSTATION_ID
columns.comments: Indicates the workstation where this operation is executed. It is a foreign key to the WIS_WORKSTATIONS_B table.

columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

objects.name: WIS_WD_OPERATIONS_B_
objects.description: This table is used to define the list of sequenced operations that are necessary to manufacture the specified product.

columns.name: WD_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a work definition operation. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_ID
columns.comments: Represents the work definition identifier that is the foreign key to the WIS_WORK_DEFINITIONS table.

columns.name: OPERATION_TYPE
columns.comments: Specifies the type of the operation. Valid values are contained within the ORA_WIS_OPERATION_TYPE lookup.

columns.name: OPERATION_SEQ_NUMBER
columns.comments: Indicates the execution sequence of the operation.

columns.name: WORK_CENTER_ID
columns.comments: Indicates the work center where this operation is executed.

columns.name: EFFECTIVE_FROM_DATE
columns.comments: Indicates the date from which this operation is effective.

columns.name: EFFECTIVE_TO_DATE
columns.comments: Indicates the date from which this operation is no longer effective.

columns.name: COUNT_POINT_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate if this is a count point operation. If an operation is a count point operation, then you have to manually complete it. Any operations in between the count points are automatically completed (i.e. backflushed, etc.).

columns.name: AUTO_TRANSACT_FLAG
columns.comments: Indicates whether both resources and materials are automatically charged based on the supply type or the charge type setups for the operation. If the supply type is Operation Pull, the component level issue transactions will happen when the operation is completed. If the supply type is Assembly Pull, the component level issue transactions will happen at the assembly completion event. Resource transactions are automatically done when the quantity is moved outside the operation. Valid values are 'Y' and 'N'.

columns.name: SERIAL_TRACKING_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate that the product is tracked by serial number while executing this operation.

columns.name: APPLICABILITY_RULE_ID
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate whether the operation is dependent on the choice of one or multiple optional components. This applies to an ATO Model work definition only.

columns.name: OPTION_DEPENDENT_FLAG
columns.comments: Indicates whether the operation is dependent on the choice of one or multiple optional components. This applies to an ATO Model work definition only.

columns.name: PLANNING_PERCENT
columns.comments: Percentage used by planning for resources forecast explosion. This applies to an ATO Model work definition only.

columns.name: REFERENCED_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate whether this operation references a standard operation.

columns.name: STANDARD_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: Represents the standard operation identifier that is the foreign key to the WIS_STANDARD_OPERATIONS_B table.

columns.name: SHIPPING_DOCUMENTS_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to determine whether shipping documents need to be generated for a supplier operation. Valid Values: 'Y' and 'N'.

columns.name: OSP_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: Item that represents the value added service in a supplier operation. This is also commonly known as a partially finished assembly.

columns.name: SUPPLIER_ID
columns.comments: Represents the identifier of the suggested supplier for a supplier operation.

columns.name: SUPPLIER_SITE_ID
columns.comments: Represents the identifier of the suggested supplier site for a supplier operation.

columns.name: LEAD_TIME_UOM
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure for the fixed and/or variable lead time values on the supplier operation.

columns.name: FIXED_LEAD_TIME
columns.comments: Represents the fixed lead time used to calculate the operation's start and end date for the supplier operation.

columns.name: VARIABLE_LEAD_TIME
columns.comments: Represents the variable lead time used to calculate the operation's start and end date based on the operation quantity for the supplier operation.

columns.name: LEAD_TIME_PERCENT
columns.comments: Represents the offset percent used in lead time roll up to calculate the cumulative lead times.

columns.name: ACTION_STATUS_CODE
columns.comments: A code used to represent the last action performed on the work definition operation which caused it to trigger the approvals workflow. Valid values are CREATE and DELETE. An empty/null value indicates this record has been reviewed and approved.

columns.name: ADDL_MTL_AT_MANUAL_ISSUE
columns.comments: Indicates whether or not this operation allows additional materials to be added at manual issue. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_ADDL_MANUAL_ISSUE_OPTS.

columns.name: OP_COMPL_WITH_UNDER_ISSUE
columns.comments: Indicates whether or not to allow operation completions with under issued material. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_OP_COMPLETION_VAL_OPTS.

columns.name: OP_COMPL_WITH_OPEN_EXCEPTIONS
columns.comments: Indicates whether or not to allow operation completions with open exceptions. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_OP_COMPLETION_VAL_OPTS.

columns.name: RESEQUENCE_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate if the operation can be re-sequenced while executing the operation. Valid values are Y or N.

columns.name: OP_YIELD_FACTOR
columns.comments: Indicates the yield factor which represents the percentage of the starting quantity that is actually yielded at the completion of the operation. The default value is 1 (100%).

columns.name: LINE_OP_SEQ_NUMBER
columns.comments: Indicates the production line operation sequence number.

columns.name: WORK_INSTRUCTION_REQUIRED_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate if a operation has a mandatory work instruction.

columns.name: ENFORCE_INSTRUCTIONS
columns.comments: Indicates whether the instructions associated with the operation are optional, required once, or required at every completion. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_INSTRUCTIONS_ENFORCE.

columns.name: CHANGE_LINE_ID
columns.comments: A unique identifier of a change order line. This is the change order line for the work definition to which the operation belongs. This is a foreign key to change_line_id of ego_change_lines_b.

columns.name: IMPLEMENTATION_DATE
columns.comments: Represents the date on which the change order line is scheduled to be implemented.

columns.name: CHANGE_BIT_MAP
columns.comments: Attribute indicating attribute changed value. Default value is 0.

columns.name: ACD_TYPE
columns.comments: Attribute indicating change affected by change order. Valid values are ADD/DELETE/UPDATE/COPY.

columns.name: OLD_WD_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: Identifier of the original work definition operation row the change order affects.

columns.name: WORKSTATION_ID
columns.comments: Indicates the workstation where this operation is executed. It is a foreign key to the WIS_WORKSTATIONS_B table.

columns.comments: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

objects.name: WIS_WD_OPERATION_MATERIALS
objects.description: This table associates an operation to one or more material lines. It defines the material consumed and/or yielded for the given operation. Note that a given material line can be consumed/yielded by/from different operations. In this case, the material quantity consumed/yielded for the operation is also maintained in this table.

columns.name: WD_OPERATION_MATERIAL_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a work definition operation material. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: MATERIAL_SEQ_NUMBER
columns.comments: Indicates the sequence of this material line within this operation.

columns.name: MATERIAL_TYPE
columns.comments: Type of material consumed by the operation. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_WD_INPUT_MATERIAL.

columns.name: MATERIAL_QUANTITY
columns.comments: This is the quantity required to produce one unit of finished goods. In the case of an ATO model, this field will not be populated and instead fetched directly from PIM.

columns.name: UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure code of the material quantity.

columns.name: YIELD_FACTOR
columns.comments: This is the percentage of material quantity actually incorporated into the finished good.

columns.name: INVERSE_MATERIAL_QUANTITY
columns.comments: Indicates the inverse quantity of material.

columns.name: BASIS_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates whether the item quantity is fixed (i.e. quantity per lot produced) or variable (i.e. quantity per item produced). Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = EGP_BOM_BASIS_TYPE.

columns.name: SUPPLY_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates the supply type code. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = EGP_WIP_SUP_TYPE.

columns.name: ADHOC_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate whether this material line is based on the item structure.

columns.name: WD_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: Reference to the operation to which this material line is assigned.

columns.name: COMPONENT_SEQUENCE_ID
columns.comments: Reference to the item structure component (EGP_COMPONENTS_B) assigned to this operation.

columns.name: COMPONENT_SEQUENCE_ID_PATH
columns.comments: Contains the lineage key of this component in the ATO Model item structure. This attribute refers to EGP_EXPLOSIONS_V.COMP_SEQ_PATH. It is used to uniquely identify this component in the exploded ATO Model item structure.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: The organization identifier that represents the manufacturing plant to which this item belongs.

columns.name: INVENTORY_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: Represents the unique identifier of the item for this material line.

columns.name: SUPPLY_SUBINVENTORY_NAME
columns.comments: Indicates the subinventory from which this material line is consumed.

columns.name: SUPPLY_LOCATOR_ID
columns.comments: Indicates the locator from which this material line is consumed.

columns.name: ENFORCE_INT_REQUIREMENTS
columns.comments: Enforce integer requirement for component's calculated quantity or inverse quantity. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = EGP_SUB_COMP_ENFORCE_INT_REQ. Valid values include: 0 - None - Do not convert to an integer. 1 - Round down - Round it down to the nearest lower integer. 2 - Round up - Round it up to the nearest higher integer.

columns.name: PREFERRED_GRADE_CODE
columns.comments: Preferred grade code for grade-controlled items used to record product completions or select item issues for a recipe, work definition or work order.

columns.name: CHANGE_LINE_ID
columns.comments: A unique identifier of a change order line. This is the change order line for the work definition to which the operation material belongs. This is a foreign key to change_line_id of ego_change_lines_b.

columns.name: IMPLEMENTATION_DATE
columns.comments: Represents the date on which the change order line is scheduled to be implemented.

columns.name: CHANGE_BIT_MAP
columns.comments: Attribute indicating attribute changed value. Default value is 0.

columns.name: ACD_TYPE
columns.comments: Attribute indicating change affected by change order. Valid values are ADD/DELETE/UPDATE/COPY.

columns.name: OLD_WD_OP_MATERIAL_ID
columns.comments: Identifier of the original work definition operation material row the change order affects.

objects.name: WIS_WD_OP_DEPENDENCIES
objects.description: This table is used to define the parallel operation dependencies setup that are necessary to manufacture the specified product.

columns.name: WD_OP_DEPENDENCY_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a work operation dependency setup. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_ID
columns.comments: Represents the work definition identifier that is the foreign key to the WIS_WORK_DEFINITIONS table.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_VERSION_ID
columns.comments: Represents the work definition version identifier that is the foreign key to the WIS_WD_VERSIONS table.

columns.name: PREVIOUS_WD_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: Represents the previous work operation identifier in the operation dependency setup. A null value in this column represents the start of the operation dependency setup. This is the foreign key to the WIS_WD_OPERATIONS_B table.

columns.name: NEXT_WD_OPERATION_ID
columns.comments: Represents the next work operation identifier in the operation dependency setup. A null value in this column represents the end of the operation dependency setup. This is the foreign key to the WIS_WD_OPERATIONS_B table.

columns.name: DEPENDENCY_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates the dependency type between previous and next work operations in the operation dependency setup. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_DEPENDENCY_TYPE.

columns.name: TRANSFER_PERCENT
columns.comments: Indicates the percent of batch quantity that is transferred between previous and next work operation in the operation dependency setup. For the first operation dependency if the batch quantity is of type calculated batch quantity, the transfer percentage is left null. For the last operation dependency, the transfer percentage is left null.

columns.name: STATUS_CODE
columns.comments: Indicates the validation status of the record. It is used internally by process manufacturing for knowing the status of processing the dependencies between operations. Possible values are ERROR - denotes that record has validation errors that need to be resolved, null - denotes that the record is clean of validation errors.

columns.name: ERROR_CODE
columns.comments: Identifies the validation error that this operation dependency record is facing. This value maps to the MESSAGE_NAME column of the FND_MESSAGES table.

columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.comments: Enterprise Service Scheduler: indicates the request ID of the job that created or last updated the row.

columns.name: JOB_DEFINITION_NAME
columns.comments: Enterprise Service Scheduler: indicates the name of the job that created or last updated the row.

columns.name: JOB_DEFINITION_PACKAGE
columns.comments: Enterprise Service Scheduler: indicates the package name of the job that created or last updated the row.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_VERSION_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a work definition version. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Indicates the version of the work definition.

It is then defaulted as shown in the work definition header where it can be edited. Maintaining the costing output batch size in the work definition allows for changes from year to year, whereas, the value in the item master is static. This costing attribute is used for cost planning and simulation purposes.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID

columns.name: COMPLETION_SUBINVENTORY_NAME

columns.name: MAXIMUM_BATCH_QUANTITY

columns.name: PARALLEL_OPS_STATUS_CODE

objects.name: WIS_WORK_CENTERS_B
objects.description: This table stores the plant specific work center definition. A work center is a physical location designated within the work area where a certain type of operation is performed. Examples are: 'Milling Center' and 'Glue Station'.

columns.name: WORK_CENTER_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a work center. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.comments: A code that represents the user key to the work center.

columns.name: INACTIVE_DATE
columns.comments: The date on which this work center has become inactive. If no date is specified, the work center is considered active.

columns.name: WORK_AREA_ID
columns.comments: Indicates the work area for which this work center is defined.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: The organization identifier that represents the manufacturing plant to which this work center belongs.

columns.name: OVERRIDE_CALENDAR_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate if this work center has overridden the plant level calendar by defining one or more work center specific calendars. Work center specific calendars are stored in the WIS_WC_PROD_CALENDARS table. A value of null or 'N' indicates that this work center has not overridden the plant level production calendar. A value of 'Y' indicates the plant level production calendar has been overridden.

columns.name: HCM_DEPARTMENT_ID
columns.comments: This attribute maps the Work Center definition to the Department that is defined in Workforce Scheduling application in HCM.

columns.name: MANUAL_WIP_MOVEMENT_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate if this work center enables staging WIP for operations executed at the work center. Valid values: Y, N, or NULL (treated as N). If Y, users are able to manually move completed quantities from one operation to the next, providing finer control over production flow and visibility of in-transit WIP.

objects.name: WIS_WORK_DEFINITIONS
objects.description: This table stores a definition of how to produce a final product with a predefined ordered set of operations, and what material and labor are required at every operation step. Examples are recipe to manufacture a pill and how to build a computer. It identifies the primary product and can optionally refer to the item structure used to define material requirements. This table also holds immutable attributes, or attributes that do not require being version controlled. Version controlled work definition attributes are stored in the work definition versions table.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a work definition. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates the type of this work definition. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_WORK_DEFINITION_TYPE.

columns.name: WORK_METHOD_ID
columns.comments: Represents the work method for which this work definition is applicable. It is a foreign key to the WIS_WORK_METHODS_B table.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: The organization identifier that represents the manufacturing plant to which this work definition belongs.

columns.name: INVENTORY_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: Represents the top level, final assembly, subassembly, or model item which belongs to the given organization.

columns.name: TRANSFORM_FROM_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: Refers to the assembly item that is being transformed to a new assembly item on a Transform work definition.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_NAME_ID
columns.comments: Represents the work definition name assigned to this work definition which is a foreign key to the WIS_WORK_DEFINITION_NAMES_B table.

columns.name: WD_MNT_NAME_ID
columns.comments: Represents the foreign key to the maintenance work definition names table.

columns.name: STATUS_CODE
columns.comments: Indicates the status of this work definition. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_WD_STATUS.

columns.name: INACTIVE_DATE
columns.comments: The date on which this work definition has become inactive.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_HEADER_NAME
columns.comments: Indicates the unique name for the work definition. In the case of process manufacturing, this represents the process name.

columns.name: PRODUCTION_PRIORITY
columns.comments: Indicates the relative rank of the work definition compared to other work definitions for the item. The work definition with a priority of '1' for an item is considered the primary work definition. A stacked rank of production priorities indicates alternate capacity to Fusion Planning.

columns.name: COSTING_PRIORITY
columns.comments: Costing uses the highest priority work definition to calculate the standard cost using the cost rollup. Upon exploding the BOM the child work definitions are threaded using the priority number chosen at the very top.

columns.name: SERIAL_TRACKING_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate that the end item (i.e. assembly in discrete manufacturing) is tracked by serial numbers during work execution.

columns.name: BILL_SEQUENCE_ID
columns.comments: Represents the item structure used to define material requirements.

columns.name: QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the quantity produced for the work definition. In process manufacturing, this is the batch quantity.

columns.name: UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure code of the work definition quantity.

columns.name: SYSTEM_GENERATED_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to identify if the work definition was automatically created by the system. Valid values: 'Y' and 'N'.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_TYPE
columns.comments: The default work order type to be used during work order creation. Valid manufacturing work order types are contained within the ORA_WIE_WO_TYPE lookup. Valid maintenance work order types are contained within the ORA_MNT_WO_TYPE lookup.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_SUB_TYPE
columns.comments: The default work order subtype to be used during work order creation. Valid manufacturing work order subtypes are contained within the ORA_WIE_WO_SUB_TYPE lookup. Valid maintenance work order subtypes are contained within the ORA_MNT_WO_SUB_TYPE lookup.

columns.name: PREASSIGN_LOT_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate that the lots for primary product and outputs can be pre-assigned in the work order.

columns.name: RESEQUENCE_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate if the work definition has re-sequence operations. Valid values are Y or N.

columns.name: MINIMUM_TRANSFER_QUANTITY
columns.comments: The minimum quantity that must be completed from the prior operation or work order before the next operation or work order is allowed to start.

columns.name: PRODUCTION_LINE_ID
columns.comments: Represents the foreign key to the WIS_PRODUCTION_LINES_B table.

columns.name: MNT_COMPLETE_TO_INV_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag indicating that the asset(s) involved in the work order will be completing to inventory upon completion of work. Its value defaults to the work order during work order creation. Valid values are Y or N.

columns.name: MNT_OUT_OF_SEQUENCE_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag indicating whether operations within the work order can be soft completed in an out of sequence fashion. Its value defaults to the work order during work order creation. Valid values are Y or N.

columns.name: PROCESS_BATCH_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates how the batch quantity is calculated for a process work definition. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_PROCESS_BATCH_QTY_TYPE.

columns.name: ENABLE_PARALLEL_OPS_FLAG
columns.comments: A flag that indicates whether parallel operations are enabled for this Work Definition. Valid values for the flag are: N or null - denotes parallel operations are not enabled, Y - denotes parallel operations are enabled.

columns.name: COMMON_WORK_DEFINITION_ID
columns.comments: Reference to the unique identifier of the global work definition created in the master organization.

columns.name: LAST_SYNC_DATE
columns.comments: Represents the date/time this record was last synchronized with the referenced work definitions.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE

objects.name: WIS_WORK_DEFINITIONS_
objects.description: This table stores a definition of how to produce a final product with a predefined ordered set of operations, and what material and labor are required at every operation step. Examples are recipe to manufacture a pill and how to build a computer. It identifies the primary product and can optionally refer to the item structure used to define material requirements. This table also holds immutable attributes, or attributes that do not require being version controlled. Version controlled work definition attributes are stored in the work definition versions table.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_ID
columns.comments: The unique identifier of a work definition. Its value is an application generated unique id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates the type of this work definition. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_WORK_DEFINITION_TYPE.

columns.name: WORK_METHOD_ID
columns.comments: Represents the work method for which this work definition is applicable. It is a foreign key to the WIS_WORK_METHODS_B table.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: The organization identifier that represents the manufacturing plant to which this work definition belongs.

columns.name: INVENTORY_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: Represents the top level, final assembly, subassembly, or model item which belongs to the given organization.

columns.name: TRANSFORM_FROM_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: Refers to the assembly item that is being transformed to a new assembly item on a Transform work definition.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_NAME_ID
columns.comments: Represents the work definition name assigned to this work definition which is a foreign key to the WIS_WORK_DEFINITION_NAMES_B table.

columns.name: WD_MNT_NAME_ID
columns.comments: Represents the foreign key to the maintenance work definition names table.

columns.name: STATUS_CODE
columns.comments: Indicates the status of this work definition. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_WD_STATUS.

columns.name: INACTIVE_DATE
columns.comments: The date on which this work definition has become inactive.

columns.name: WORK_DEFINITION_HEADER_NAME
columns.comments: Indicates the unique name for the work definition. In the case of process manufacturing, this represents the process name.

columns.name: PRODUCTION_PRIORITY
columns.comments: Indicates the relative rank of the work definition compared to other work definitions for the item. The work definition with a priority of '1' for an item is considered the primary work definition. A stacked rank of production priorities indicates alternate capacity to Fusion Planning.

columns.name: COSTING_PRIORITY
columns.comments: Costing uses the highest priority work definition to calculate the standard cost using the cost rollup. Upon exploding the BOM the child work definitions are threaded using the priority number chosen at the very top.

columns.name: SERIAL_TRACKING_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate that the end item (i.e. assembly in discrete manufacturing) is tracked by serial numbers during work execution.

columns.name: BILL_SEQUENCE_ID
columns.comments: Represents the item structure used to define material requirements.

columns.name: QUANTITY
columns.comments: Represents the quantity produced for the work definition. In process manufacturing, this is the batch quantity.

columns.name: UOM_CODE
columns.comments: Represents the unit of measure code of the work definition quantity.

columns.name: SYSTEM_GENERATED_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to identify if the work definition was automatically created by the system. Valid values: 'Y' and 'N'.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_TYPE
columns.comments: The default work order type to be used during work order creation. Valid manufacturing work order types are contained within the ORA_WIE_WO_TYPE lookup. Valid maintenance work order types are contained within the ORA_MNT_WO_TYPE lookup.

columns.name: WORK_ORDER_SUB_TYPE
columns.comments: The default work order subtype to be used during work order creation. Valid manufacturing work order subtypes are contained within the ORA_WIE_WO_SUB_TYPE lookup. Valid maintenance work order subtypes are contained within the ORA_MNT_WO_SUB_TYPE lookup.

columns.name: PREASSIGN_LOT_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate that the lots for primary product and outputs can be pre-assigned in the work order.

columns.name: RESEQUENCE_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag used to indicate if the work definition has re-sequence operations. Valid values are Y or N.

columns.name: MINIMUM_TRANSFER_QUANTITY
columns.comments: The minimum quantity that must be completed from the prior operation or work order before the next operation or work order is allowed to start.

columns.name: PRODUCTION_LINE_ID
columns.comments: Represents the foreign key to the WIS_PRODUCTION_LINES_B table.

columns.name: MNT_COMPLETE_TO_INV_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag indicating that the asset(s) involved in the work order will be completing to inventory upon completion of work. Its value defaults to the work order during work order creation. Valid values are Y or N.

columns.name: MNT_OUT_OF_SEQUENCE_FLAG
columns.comments: Flag indicating whether operations within the work order can be soft completed in an out of sequence fashion. Its value defaults to the work order during work order creation. Valid values are Y or N.

columns.name: PROCESS_BATCH_TYPE
columns.comments: Indicates how the batch quantity is calculated for a process work definition. Valid values exist in the lookup with lookup type = ORA_WIS_PROCESS_BATCH_QTY_TYPE.

columns.name: ENABLE_PARALLEL_OPS_FLAG
columns.comments: A flag that indicates whether parallel operations are enabled for this Work Definition. Valid values for the flag are: N or null - denotes parallel operations are not enabled, Y - denotes parallel operations are enabled.

columns.name: COMMON_WORK_DEFINITION_ID
columns.comments: Reference to the unique identifier of the global work definition created in the master organization.

columns.comments: Represents the date/time this record was last synchronized with the referenced work definitions.

objects.name: WIS_COMMON_WD_OPERATIONS_V
objects.query:
SELECT wdo.wd_operation_id,
wdo.operation_seq_number,
wdo.work_definition_id,
wdv.version_number
FROM wis_wd_operations_b wdo,
wis_wd_versions wdv
WHERE wdv.work_definition_id = wdo.work_definition_id
AND wdv.effective_from_date between wdo.effective_from_date and nvl(wdo.effective_to_date, wdv.effective_from_date)
AND (systimestamp between wdv.effective_from_date and nvl(wdv.effective_to_date,sysdate+1)
OR
wdv.effective_from_date >= systimestamp)
AND wdo.referenced_flag = 'N'

objects.name: WIS_COMMON_WORK_DEFINITIONS_V
objects.query:
SELECT wd.work_definition_id work_definition_id,
wm.work_method_code work_method_code,
wd.organization_id organization_id,
iop.organization_code organization_code,
wd.inventory_item_id inventory_item_id,
esi.item_number item_number,
wdn.work_definition_code work_definition_code
FROM wis_work_definitions wd,
wis_work_methods_b wm,
inv_org_parameters iop,
egp_system_items_bv esi,
wis_work_definition_names_b wdn
WHERE wm.work_method_code IN ('DISCRETE_MANUFACTURING', 'PROCESS_MANUFACTURING')
AND wd.work_method_id = wm.work_method_id
AND wd.system_generated_flag = 'N'
AND wd.status_code <> 'INACTIVE'
AND iop.organization_id = wd.organization_id
AND esi.inventory_item_id = wd.inventory_item_id
AND esi.organization_id = wd.organization_id
AND wdn.work_definition_name_id = wd.work_definition_name_id
AND ( EXISTS(
SELECT 'Y' FROM wis_wd_versions wdv,
edr_signature_organization eso,
edr_signature_definitions esd
WHERE wdv.work_definition_id = wd.work_definition_id
AND eso.organization_id = wdv.organization_id
AND esd.signature_organization_id = eso.signature_organization_id
AND esd.transaction_type_code = 'WORK_DEFINITION'
AND esd.signature_enabled_flag = 'Y'
AND wdv.approval_status_code = 'DRAFT')
OR
NOT EXISTS (
SELECT 'Y' FROM edr_signature_organization eso1,
edr_signature_definitions esd1
WHERE eso1.organization_id = wd.organization_id
AND esd1.signature_organization_id = eso1.signature_organization_id
AND esd1.signature_enabled_flag = 'Y'))
UNION
SELECT wd.work_definition_id,
wm.work_method_code,
wd.organization_id,
iop.organization_code,
null,
null,
wdmn.maintenance_wd_code
FROM wis_work_definitions wd,
wis_work_methods_b wm,
inv_org_parameters iop,
wis_wd_maintenance_names_b wdmn
WHERE wm.work_method_code = 'MAINTENANCE'
AND wd.work_method_id = wm.work_method_id
AND iop.organization_id = wd.organization_id
AND wdmn.wd_mnt_name_id = wd.wd_mnt_name_id

TO_CHAR(COMP.BASIS_TYPE) as BASIS_TYPE,
NVL(MTL.UOM_CODE, COMP.PRIMARY_UOM_CODE) UOM_CODE,
MTL.SUPPLY_TYPE,
CASE WHEN MTL.COMPONENT_SEQUENCE_ID_PATH IS NULL
THEN MTL.MATERIAL_QUANTITY
ELSE COMP.COMPONENT_QUANTITY END MATERIAL_QUANTITY,
CASE WHEN MTL.COMPONENT_SEQUENCE_ID_PATH IS NULL
THEN MTL.INVERSE_MATERIAL_QUANTITY
ELSE decode(COMP.COMPONENT_QUANTITY,0,0,wie_int_utils_pvt.round_precision(1/COMP.COMPONENT_QUANTITY)) END INVERSE_MATERIAL_QUANTITY,
MTL.SUPPLY_SUBINVENTORY_NAME,
MTL.SUPPLY_LOCATOR_ID,
MTL.ACD_TYPE AS MTL_ACD_TYPE,
MTL.OLD_WD_OP_MATERIAL_ID,
COMP.OPTIONAL,
COMP.PLANNING_FACTOR,
TO_CHAR(COMP.ENFORCE_INT_REQUIREMENTS),
COMP.CHECK_ATP,
COMP.EFFECTIVITY_DATE,
COMP.DISABLE_DATE,
COMP.COMPONENT_QUANTITY,
COMP.ITEM_NUM,
COMP.QUANTITY_RELATED,
COMP.SO_BASIS,
COMP.MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE_OPTIONS,
COMP.LOW_QUANTITY,
COMP.HIGH_QUANTITY,
COMP.BOM_ITEM_TYPE,
COMP.OPTIONAL_ON_MODEL,
COMP.ACD_TYPE,
COMP.OPERATION_SEQ_NUM AS FIND_NUMBER,
ITEM.PRIMARY_UOM_CODE,
COMP.CONTRIBUTE_TO_YIELD AS CONTRIBUTE_TO_YIELD_FLAG,
MTL.PREFERRED_GRADE_CODE
FROM
WIS_WORK_DEFINITIONS WD,
WIS_WD_OPERATIONS_B WDO,
WIS_WD_OPERATION_MATERIALS MTL,
EGP_SYSTEM_ITEMS_VL ITEM,
EGP_COMPONENTS_B COMP
WHERE NVL(WD.SYSTEM_GENERATED_FLAG,'N')='N'
AND MTL.ADHOC_FLAG = 'N'
AND WD.WORK_DEFINITION_ID = WDO.WORK_DEFINITION_ID
AND WDO.WD_OPERATION_ID = MTL.WD_OPERATION_ID
AND WD.ORGANIZATION_ID = MTL.ORGANIZATION_ID
AND MTL.COMPONENT_SEQUENCE_ID = COMP.COMPONENT_SEQUENCE_ID
AND MTL.INVENTORY_ITEM_ID = COMP.PK1_VALUE
AND COMP.PK1_VALUE = ITEM.INVENTORY_ITEM_ID
AND COMP.PK2_VALUE = ITEM.ORGANIZATION_ID
AND COMP.IMPLEMENTATION_DATE IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT
MTL.ROWID ROW_ID,
MTL.WD_OPERATION_MATERIAL_ID,
MTL.MATERIAL_SEQ_NUMBER,
MTL.MATERIAL_TYPE,
MTL.ADHOC_FLAG,
MTL.COMPONENT_SEQUENCE_ID,
MTL.COMPONENT_SEQUENCE_ID_PATH,
MTL.WD_OPERATION_ID,
WD.WORK_DEFINITION_ID,
MTL.ORGANIZATION_ID,
MTL.INVENTORY_ITEM_ID,

NULL AS ITEM_NUM,
NULL AS QUANTITY_RELATED,
NULL AS SO_BASIS,

NULL AS LOW_QUANTITY,

NULL AS OPTIONAL_ON_MODEL,
NULL AS ACD_TYPE,
NULL AS FIND_NUMBER,
ITEM.PRIMARY_UOM_CODE,

MTL.PREFERRED_GRADE_CODE
FROM
WIS_WORK_DEFINITIONS WD,
WIS_WD_OPERATIONS_B WDO,
WIS_WD_OPERATION_MATERIALS MTL,
EGP_SYSTEM_ITEMS_VL ITEM
WHERE NVL(WD.SYSTEM_GENERATED_FLAG,'N')='N'
AND MTL.ADHOC_FLAG = 'Y'
AND WD.WORK_DEFINITION_ID = WDO.WORK_DEFINITION_ID
AND WDO.WD_OPERATION_ID = MTL.WD_OPERATION_ID
AND WD.ORGANIZATION_ID = MTL.ORGANIZATION_ID
AND MTL.COMPONENT_SEQUENCE_ID IS NULL
AND MTL.INVENTORY_ITEM_ID = ITEM.INVENTORY_ITEM_ID
AND MTL.ORGANIZATION_ID = ITEM.ORGANIZATION_ID
UNION ALL

||TO_CHAR(ROUND(1/COMP.COMPONENT_QUANTITY,PRECISION_VAL.PROFILE_OPTION_VALUE)),TO_CHAR(ROUND(1/COMP.COMPONENT_QUANTITY,PRECISION_VAL.PROFILE_OPTION_VALUE)))))) AS INVERSE_MATERIAL_QUANTITY,

COMP.SUPPLY_LOCATOR_ID,

NULL AS OLD_WD_OP_MATERIAL_ID,
COMP.OPTIONAL,
COMP.PLANNING_FACTOR,
TO_CHAR(COMP.ENFORCE_INT_REQUIREMENTS),
COMP.CHECK_ATP,
COMP.EFFECTIVITY_DATE,
COMP.DISABLE_DATE,
COMP.COMPONENT_QUANTITY,
COMP.ITEM_NUM,
COMP.QUANTITY_RELATED,
COMP.SO_BASIS,
COMP.MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE_OPTIONS,
COMP.LOW_QUANTITY,
COMP.HIGH_QUANTITY,
COMP.BOM_ITEM_TYPE,
COMP.OPTIONAL_ON_MODEL,
COMP.ACD_TYPE,
COMP.OPERATION_SEQ_NUM AS FIND_NUMBER,
ITEM.PRIMARY_UOM_CODE,
COMP.CONTRIBUTE_TO_YIELD AS CONTRIBUTE_TO_YIELD_FLAG,
NULL AS PREFERRED_GRADE_CODE
FROM
WIS_WORK_DEFINITIONS WD,
WIS_WD_OPERATIONS_B WDO,
EGP_SYSTEM_ITEMS_VL ITEM,
EGP_COMPONENTS_B COMP,
EGP_STRUCTURES_B STRT,
(SELECT NVL(PROFILE_OPTION_VALUE,5) PROFILE_OPTION_VALUE FROM FND_PROFILE_OPTION_VALUES VAL, FND_PROFILE_OPTIONS_VL PF

objects.name: WIS_WD_OP_DEP_OP_YIELD_V
objects.query:
WITH wm AS (
SELECT /*+ materialize */
work_method_id
FROM
wis_work_methods_b
WHERE
work_method_code = 'PROCESS_MANUFACTURING'
), wd_op_dep AS (
SELECT
wdo.work_definition_id AS wd_id,
wdo.operation_seq_number,
wdv.version_number,
wdv.work_definition_version_id wd_ver_id,
opdep.previous_wd_operation_id AS prev_op,
opdep.next_wd_operation_id AS curr_op,
nvl(opdep.transfer_percent, 100) AS transfer_pct, /* set default to 100 */
CASE
WHEN wdo.referenced_flag = 'Y' THEN
nvl(stdo.op_yield_factor, 1.0)
ELSE
nvl(wdo.op_yield_factor, 1.0)
END op_yield /* set default to 1 */
FROM
wis_wd_operations_b wdo,
wis_standard_operations_b stdo,
wis_wd_versions wdv,
wm,
wis_work_definitions wd,
wis_wd_op_dependencies opdep
WHERE
wdv.work_definition_id = wdo.work_definition_id
AND wdo.standard_operation_id = stdo.standard_operation_id (+)
AND wdv.work_definition_id = wd.work_definition_id
AND wd.enable_parallel_ops_flag = 'Y' /* Only for enforce dep WDs. */
AND wd.work_method_id = wm.work_method_id /* Only for Process Work Methods */
AND wdo.work_definition_id = opdep.work_definition_id
AND wdv.work_definition_version_id = opdep.work_definition_version_id
AND wdo.wd_operation_id = nvl(opdep.next_wd_operation_id, opdep.previous_wd_operation_id)
AND opdep.dependency_type = 'ORA_FINISH_TO_START' /* Include only Finish to Start deps */
), wd_op_dep_a AS (
SELECT /*+ materialize */
*
FROM
wd_op_dep
WHERE
curr_op IS NOT NULL
), branches_rec (
wd_id,
wd_ver_id,
version_number,
prev_op,
curr_op,
operation_seq_number,
transfer_pct,
op_yield,
net_yld,
net_transfer_pct
) AS (
SELECT
wd_id,
wd_ver_id,
version_number,
prev_op,
curr_op,
operation_seq_number,
transfer_pct,
op_yield,
ln(transfer_pct / 100) + ln(op_yield) AS net_yld,
ln(transfer_pct / 100) AS net_transfer_pct
FROM
wd_op_dep_a
WHERE
prev_op IS NULL /* starting point */
UNION ALL
SELECT /* leading(dep b) */
dep.wd_id,
dep.wd_ver_id,
dep.version_number,
dep.prev_op,
dep.curr_op,
dep.operation_seq_number,
dep.transfer_pct,
dep.op_yield,
b.net_yld + ln(dep.transfer_pct / 100) + ln(dep.op_yield) AS net_yld,
b.net_transfer_pct + ln(dep.transfer_pct / 100) AS net_transfer_pct
FROM
wd_op_dep_a dep,
branches_rec b
WHERE
b.wd_id = dep.wd_id
AND b.wd_ver_id = dep.wd_ver_id
AND b.curr_op = dep.prev_op
)
CYCLE wd_id, wd_ver_id, curr_op SET is_cycle TO 1 DEFAULT 0, fwd_yields AS (
SELECT
wd_id,
wd_ver_id,
version_number,
curr_op,
operation_seq_number,
op_yield,
SUM(exp(net_yld)) AS fwd_yld,
SUM(exp(net_transfer_pct)) AS fwd_transfer_pct
FROM
branches_rec
GROUP BY
wd_id,
wd_ver_id,
version_number,
curr_op,
operation_seq_number,
op_yield
), final_yield AS (
SELECT
fy.wd_id,
fy.wd_ver_id,
fy.curr_op,
fy.fwd_yld AS net_yield
FROM
fwd_yields fy,
(
SELECT
wd_id,
wd_ver_id,
prev_op
FROM
wd_op_dep
WHERE
curr_op IS NULL
) depops
WHERE
depops.wd_id = fy.wd_id
AND depops.wd_ver_id = fy.wd_ver_id
AND depops.prev_op = fy.curr_op
)
SELECT
fw.curr_op wd_operation_id,
fw.operation_seq_number operation_seq_number,
fw.wd_id work_definition_id,
fw.wd_ver_id work_definition_version_id,
fw.version_number version_number,
fw.op_yield op_yield_factor,
round(fw.fwd_yld, 30) cumulative_yield,
round((fy.net_yield / nvl(fw.fwd_yld, 1.0)) * fw.op_yield,
30) rev_cumulative_yield,
round(fw.fwd_transfer_pct * 100, 30) cumulative_transfer_pct,
round((fw.fwd_yld / nvl((fw.op_yield * fw.fwd_transfer_pct), 1.0)),
30) input_scale_factor,
round((fw.fwd_yld / nvl(fw.fwd_transfer_pct, 1.0)),
30) output_scale_factor
FROM
fwd_yields fw,
final_yield fy
WHERE
fw.wd_id = fy.wd_id
AND fw.wd_ver_id = fy.wd_ver_id
ORDER BY
fw.wd_id,
fw.wd_ver_id,
fw.curr_op
