objects.name: ACD_RESOURCE_B_INT
objects.description: Product Proposal Resource interface table for Bulk Import.

columns.name: RESOURCE_ID
columns.comments: Primary Key which will be system generated Application Unique Id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: PRODUCT_PROPOSAL_ID
columns.comments: Refers to Product Proposal Id from ACD_PRODUCT_PROPOSAL table as Foreign key

columns.name: RESOURCE_POOL
columns.comments: Custom lookup value for the resource pool attribute.

columns.name: RESOURCE_STATUS
columns.comments: Indicates the status of resource for Product Concept (Budgeted,Estimated,Actual) The supported types are defined in the Lookup type with the name ACD_RESOURCE_STATUS and the look up codes are BUDGETED,ESTIMATED,ACTUAL values

columns.name: RESOURCE_HEADCOUNT
columns.comments: Total resource headcount required during the time-period between start and end dates

columns.name: START_DATE
columns.comments: Start date of a time-period e.g. 04/01/2010

columns.name: END_DATE
columns.comments: End date of a time-period e.g. 08/01/2011

columns.name: RESOURCE_TREND
columns.comments: Indicates the trend of resource for Product Concept (Point, Uniformly Distributed, Front Loaded, Back Loaded) The supported types are defined in the Lookup type with the name ACD_TREND and the look up codes are POINT,UNIFORMLY_DISTRIBUTED,FRONT_LOADED,BACK_LOADED values

columns.name: RESOURCE_CATEGORY
columns.comments: Custom look up values for the resource category.

columns.name: SOURCE
columns.comments: Source for the resources fromlookup(Proposal,Project).values are PROPOSAL,PROJECT

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: NAME
columns.comments: This is the translatable Name for the Resource.

columns.name: LANG_CODE
columns.comments: Indicates the code of the language into which the contents of the translatable columns are translated.

columns.name: SRC_LANG_CODE
columns.comments: Indicates the code of the language in which the contents of the translatable columns were originally created.

columns.name: SOURCE_LANG_FLAG
columns.comments: Indicates the code of the language in which the contents of the translatable columns were originally created.

columns.name: IMPORT_STATUS_CODE
columns.comments: IMPORT_STATUS_CODE tells status of a row in the interface table.

columns.name: INTERNAL_ACTION_CODE
columns.comments: This column is created for internal use and will be populated and used by bulk import logic.

columns.name: ACTION_CODE
columns.comments: ACTION_CODE in interface table allows source system to specify a particular operation (insert, update, etc) for a row.

columns.name: LOAD_REQUEST_ID
columns.comments: When Data file uploaded and click on submit that time the load request Id generated.

columns.name: INTERFACE_ROW_ID
columns.comments: INTERFACE_ROW_ID is the unique identifier for the record with in a batch.

objects.description: This is the XM table for ACD_RESOURCE

columns.name: ID
columns.comments: This is the primary key of the table.

columns.name: RECORD_NUMBER
columns.comments: Extensibility column that stores the number of the reference entity record.

columns.name: RESOURCE_ID
columns.comments: Primary Key which will be system generated Application Unique Id.

columns.name: RECORD_NAME
columns.comments: Extensibility column that stores the name of the reference entity record.

columns.name: ATTRIBUTE_CATEGORY
columns.comments: Descriptive Flexfield: structure definition of the user descriptive flexfield.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: CONFLICT_ID
columns.comments: Disconnected Mobile: this value is used to guarantee the uniqueness of the row when duplicates are created in different databases (i.e. mobile databases or the server).

columns.name: CPDRF_VER_SOR
columns.comments: CPDRF_VER_SOR

columns.name: CPDRF_VER_PILLAR
columns.comments: CPDRF_VER_PILLAR

columns.name: CPDRF_LAST_UPD
columns.comments: CPDRF_LAST_UPD

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: USER_LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Disconnected Mobile: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row. This value is different from LAST_UPDATE_DATE if the update originally happened in a different database (i.e. a different mobile database or the server).

columns.name: REQUEST_ID
columns.comments: Enterprise Service Scheduler: indicates the request ID of the job that created or last updated the row.

columns.name: JOB_DEFINITION_NAME
columns.comments: Enterprise Service Scheduler: indicates the name of the job that created or last updated the row.

columns.name: JOB_DEFINITION_PACKAGE
columns.comments: Enterprise Service Scheduler: indicates the package name of the job that created or last updated the row.

columns.comments: Column that stores the corporate currency code.

columns.comments: Column that stores the conversion rate type for the corporate currency.

objects.name: ACD_REVENUE
objects.description: Contains detailed information for the Product Proposal Revenue Details.

columns.name: REVENUE_ID
columns.comments: Primary Key which will be system generated Application Unique Id.

columns.name: CURRENCY_CODE
columns.comments: Column that stores the currency code.

columns.name: CORP_CURRENCY_CODE
columns.comments: Column that stores the corporate currency code.

columns.name: CURCY_CONV_RATE_TYPE
columns.comments: Column that stores the conversion rate type for the corporate currency.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: PRODUCT_PROPOSAL_ID
columns.comments: Refers to Product Proposal Id from ACD_PRODUCT_PROPOSAL table as Foreign key

columns.name: REVENUE_STATUS
columns.comments: Indicates the status of revenue for Product Concept (Projected,Estimated,Actual) The supported types are defined in the Lookup type with the name ACD_REVENUE_STATUS and the look up codes are PROJECTED,ESTIMATED,ACTUAL values

columns.name: REVENUE_AMOUNT
columns.comments: Total revenue amount during the time-period between start and end dates

columns.name: START_DATE
columns.comments: Start date of a time-period e.g. 04/01/201

columns.name: END_DATE
columns.comments: End date of a time-period e.g. 08/01/2011

columns.name: REVENUE_TREND
columns.comments: Indicates the trend of revenue for Product Concept (Point, Uniformly Distributed, Front Loaded, Back Loaded) The supported types are defined in the Lookup type with the name ACD_TREND and the look up codes are POINT,UNIFORMLY_DISTRIBUTED,FRONT_LOADED,BACK_LOADED values

columns.name: REVENUE_CATEGORY
columns.comments: Indicates the category of revenue for Product Concept (e.g. NA,EMEA,APAC etc) The supported types are defined in the Lookup type with the name ACD_REVENUE_CATEGORY and the look up codes are custom values

columns.name: REVENUE_TYPE
columns.comments: Custom lookup value for the revenue type.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

objects.name: ACD_REVENUE_B_INT
objects.description: Product Proposal Revenue interface table for Bulk Import.

columns.name: REVENUE_ID
columns.comments: Primary Key which will be system generated Application Unique Id.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: PRODUCT_PROPOSAL_ID
columns.comments: Refers to Product Proposal Id from ACD_PRODUCT_PROPOSAL table as Foreign key

columns.name: REVENUE_STATUS
columns.comments: Indicates the status of revenue for Product Concept (Projected,Estimated,Actual) The supported types are defined in the Lookup type with the name ACD_REVENUE_STATUS and the look up codes are PROJECTED,ESTIMATED,ACTUAL values

columns.name: REVENUE_AMOUNT
columns.comments: Total revenue amount during the time-period between start and end dates

columns.name: START_DATE
columns.comments: Start date of a time-period e.g. 04/01/2017

columns.name: END_DATE
columns.comments: End date of a time-period e.g. 08/01/2011

columns.name: REVENUE_TREND
columns.comments: Indicates the trend of revenue for Product Concept (Point, Uniformly Distributed, Front Loaded, Back Loaded) The supported types are defined in the Lookup type with the name ACD_TREND and the look up codes are POINT,UNIFORMLY_DISTRIBUTED,FRONT_LOADED,BACK_LOADED values

columns.name: REVENUE_CATEGORY
columns.comments: Indicates the category of revenue for Product Concept (e.g. NA,EMEA,APAC etc) The supported types are defined in the Lookup type with the name ACD_REVENUE_CATEGORY and the look up codes are custom values

columns.name: REVENUE_TYPE
columns.comments: Custom lookup values for the revenue type.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: NAME
columns.comments: This is the translatable NAME for the object.

columns.name: LANG_CODE
columns.comments: Indicates the code of the language into which the contents of the translatable columns are translated.

columns.name: SRC_LANG_CODE
columns.comments: Indicates the code of the language in which the contents of the translatable columns were originally created.

columns.name: SOURCE_LANG_FLAG
columns.comments: Indicates the code of the language in which the contents of the translatable columns were originally created.

columns.name: IMPORT_STATUS_CODE
columns.comments: IMPORT_STATUS_CODE tells status of a row in the interface table.

columns.name: INTERNAL_ACTION_CODE
columns.comments: This column is created for internal use and will be populated and used by bulk import logic.

columns.name: ACTION_CODE
columns.comments: ACTION_CODE in interface table allows source system to specify a particular operation (insert, update, etc) for a row.

columns.name: LOAD_REQUEST_ID
columns.comments: When Data file uploaded and click on submit that time the load request Id generated.

columns.name: INTERFACE_ROW_ID
columns.comments: INTERFACE_ROW_ID is the unique identifier for the record with in a batch.

columns.name: ID
columns.comments: This is the primary key of the table.

columns.name: RECORD_NUMBER
columns.comments: Extensibility column that stores the number of the reference entity record.

columns.name: REVENUE_ID
columns.comments: Primary Key which will be system generated Application Unique Id.

columns.comments: Extensibility column that stores the name of the reference entity record.

columns.name: ATTRIBUTE_CATEGORY
columns.comments: Descriptive Flexfield: structure definition of the user descriptive flexfield.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: CONFLICT_ID
columns.comments: Disconnected Mobile: this value is used to guarantee the uniqueness of the row when duplicates are created in different databases (i.e. mobile databases or the server).

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: USER_LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Disconnected Mobile: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row. This value is different from LAST_UPDATE_DATE if the update originally happened in a different database (i.e. a different mobile database or the server).

columns.name: REQUEST_ID
columns.comments: Enterprise Service Scheduler: indicates the request ID of the job that created or last updated the row.

columns.name: JOB_DEFINITION_NAME
columns.comments: Enterprise Service Scheduler: indicates the name of the job that created or last updated the row.

columns.name: JOB_DEFINITION_PACKAGE
columns.comments: Enterprise Service Scheduler: indicates the package name of the job that created or last updated the row.

objects.name: ACD_SOLUTION_ALTERNATIVE_B
objects.description: Contains detailed information about solution alternatives.

columns.name: SOLUTION_ALTERNATIVE_ID
columns.comments: Unique alternative ID. Each concept has a set of its own solution alternatives.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: DEFAULT_ALTERNATIVE
columns.comments: 'yes' for the default alternative, otherwise 'no'

columns.name: ALTERNATIVE_INDEX
columns.comments: Alternative index e.g. [1..15] is unique for one concept

columns.name: POSNO
columns.comments: This is the pos no of the solution alternative used for sorting purposes.

columns.name: IS_ACTIVE
columns.comments: 'y' if this alternative should be visible in the concept's structure

columns.name: IS_VISIBLE
columns.comments: 'y' if this alternative should be visible in the list of available solution alternatives, otherwise 'n'

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CONCEPT_ID
columns.comments: Reference to concept this solution alternative belongs to

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

objects.name: ACD_CONCEPTS_PROJ_TASKS_V
objects.query:
SELECT ACS.CONCEPT_STRUCTURE_ID,
SUM(
CASE
WHEN POA.OBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL
THEN 1
ELSE 0
END) AS TaskIdCount
FROM PJE_OBJECT_ASSOCIATIONS POA,
(SELECT ACS.CONCEPT_STRUCTURE_ID,
CASE
WHEN ACS.FROM_TYPE = 'CONCEPT'
THEN ACS.FROM_ID
WHEN ACS.TO_TYPE = 'CONCEPT'
THEN ACS.TO_ID
END AS RELATED_CONCEPT_ID
FROM ACD_CONCEPT_STRUCTURE ACS
WHERE CONCEPT_STRUCTURE_ID IN
(SELECT SRC_OBJ_ID
FROM aca_cs_relationship
WHERE src_obj_type = 'CONCEPT'
AND dest_obj_type = 'Projects'
)
) ACS
WHERE POA.ASSOCIATED_OBJECT_SUB_TYPE_ID IN
(SELECT DELIVERABLE_TYPE_ID
FROM PJE_DELIVERABLE_TYPES_VL CONCEPTCLASS
WHERE CONCEPTCLASS.DELIVERABLE_TYPE_CLASS='PLM_CONCEPT'
)
AND POA.ASSOCIATED_OBJECT_ID = ACS.RELATED_CONCEPT_ID
GROUP BY ACS.CONCEPT_STRUCTURE_ID

objects.name: ACD_CONCEPTS_RELATIONSHIP_V
objects.query:
SELECT ConceptRel1.RELATIONSHIP_ID,
ConceptRel1.OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER,
ConceptRel1.RELATIONSHIP_TYPE,
ConceptRel1.TARGET_TYPE,
ConceptRel1.DIRECTION_TYPE,
ConceptRel1.SRC_OBJ_TYPE,
ConceptRel1.SRC_OBJ_ID,
ConceptRel1.DEST_OBJ_TYPE,
ConceptRel1.DEST_OBJ_ID,
ConceptRel1.CREATED_BY,
ConceptRel1.CREATION_DATE,
ConceptRel1.LAST_UPDATED_BY,
ConceptRel1.LAST_UPDATE_DATE,
ConceptRel1.DERIVED_REQUIREMENT_ID,
ConceptRel1.DERIVED_IDEA_ID,
ConceptRel1.DERIVED_PROPOSAL_ID,
ConceptRel1.DERIVED_REQUIREMENT_LINE_ID,
ConceptRel1.DERIVED_COMPONENT_ID,
ConceptRel1.DERIVED_ITEM_ID,
ConceptRel1.DERIVED_PROJECTS_ID,
CASE
WHEN ConceptRel2.derived_CONCEPT_ID IS NOT NULL
THEN ConceptRel2.derived_CONCEPT_ID
WHEN ConceptRel1.derived_CONCEPT_ID IS NOT NULL
THEN ConceptRel1.derived_CONCEPT_ID
END AS FINAL_DERIVED_ID,
CASE
WHEN ConceptRel2.DRIVING_CONCEPT_ID IS NOT NULL
THEN ConceptRel2.DRIVING_CONCEPT_ID
WHEN ConceptRel1.DRIVING_CONCEPT_ID IS NOT NULL
THEN ConceptRel1.DRIVING_CONCEPT_ID
END AS FINAL_DRIVING_ID
FROM
(SELECT RELATIONSHIP_ID,
OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER,
RELATIONSHIP_TYPE,
TARGET_TYPE,
DIRECTION_TYPE,
SRC_OBJ_TYPE,
SRC_OBJ_ID,
DEST_OBJ_TYPE,
DEST_OBJ_ID,
CREATED_BY,
CREATION_DATE,
LAST_UPDATED_BY,
LAST_UPDATE_DATE,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'REQUIREMENT')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'REQUIREMENT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS DERIVED_REQUIREMENT_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'IDEA')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'IDEA'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS DERIVED_IDEA_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'PROPOSAL')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'PROPOSAL'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS DERIVED_PROPOSAL_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'REQUIREMENT_LINE_ITEM')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'REQUIREMENT_LINE_ITEM'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS DERIVED_REQUIREMENT_LINE_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'COMPONENT')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'COMPONENT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS DERIVED_COMPONENT_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'ITEM')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'ITEM'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS DERIVED_ITEM_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'Projects')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'Projects'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS DERIVED_PROJECTS_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type = 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type != 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type != 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
END AS DRIVING_CONCEPT_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type = 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type != 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type!= 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
END AS derived_CONCEPT_ID
FROM ACA_CS_RELATIONSHIP AR
WHERE SRC_OBJ_TYPE = 'CONCEPT'
OR DEST_OBJ_TYPE = 'CONCEPT'
) ConceptRel1,
(SELECT RELATIONSHIP_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
END AS derived_CONCEPT_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS DRIVING_CONCEPT_ID
FROM ACA_CS_RELATIONSHIP AR
WHERE SRC_OBJ_TYPE = 'CONCEPT'
OR DEST_OBJ_TYPE = 'CONCEPT'
UNION
SELECT RELATIONSHIP_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS derived_CONCEPT_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
END AS DRIVING_CONCEPT_ID
FROM ACA_CS_RELATIONSHIP AR
WHERE SRC_OBJ_TYPE = 'CONCEPT'
OR DEST_OBJ_TYPE = 'CONCEPT'
) ConceptRel2
WHERE ConceptRel1.RELATIONSHIP_ID = ConceptRel2.RELATIONSHIP_ID

objects.name: ACD_CONCEPTS_STRUCTURE_COUNT_V
objects.query:
SELECT connect_by_root acs.concept_structure_id concept_structure_id,
connect_by_root acs.top_concept_id top_concept_id,
connect_by_root acv.name concept_name,
connect_by_root acv.description concept_description,
connect_by_root acv.lifecycle_phase lifecycle_phase,
level distance,
CASE
WHEN acs.to_type='ITEM'
THEN acs.to_item_id
ELSE TO_CHAR(acs.to_id)
END AS related_type_id,
acs.to_type related_type,
1 AS element_count,
CASE
WHEN acs.to_type='COMPONENT'
THEN 1
ELSE 0
END AS component_count,
CASE
WHEN acs.to_type='ITEM'
THEN 1
ELSE 0
END AS item_count
FROM ACD_CONCEPT_STRUCTURE acs,
ACD_CONCEPT_VL acv
WHERE acs.top_concept_id = acv.concept_id
START WITH acs.from_str_id IS NULL
CONNECT BY prior acs.concept_structure_id = acs.from_str_id

objects.name: ACD_PROP_RELATIONSHIP_V
objects.query:
SELECT PropRel1.RELATIONSHIP_ID,
PropRel1.OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER,
PropRel1.RELATIONSHIP_TYPE,
PropRel1.TARGET_TYPE,
PropRel1.DIRECTION_TYPE,
PropRel1.SRC_OBJ_TYPE,
PropRel1.SRC_OBJ_ID,
PropRel1.DEST_OBJ_TYPE,
PropRel1.DEST_OBJ_ID,
PropRel1.CREATED_BY,
PropRel1.CREATION_DATE,
PropRel1.LAST_UPDATED_BY,
PropRel1.LAST_UPDATE_DATE,
PropRel1.DERIVED_REQUIREMENT_ID,
PropRel1.DERIVED_CONCEPT_ID,
PropRel1.DERIVED_IDEA_ID,
PropRel1.DERIVED_REQUIREMENT_LINE_ID,
PropRel1.DERIVED_COMPONENT_ID,
NULL AS DERIVED_PROJECT_ID,
NULL AS DERIVED_TASK_ID,
CASE
WHEN PropRel2.derived_PROP_ID IS NOT NULL
THEN PropRel2.derived_PROP_ID
WHEN PropRel1.derived_PROP_ID IS NOT NULL
THEN PropRel1.derived_PROP_ID
END AS FINAL_DERIVED_ID,
CASE
WHEN PropRel2.DRIVING_PROP_ID IS NOT NULL
THEN PropRel2.DRIVING_PROP_ID
WHEN PropRel1.DRIVING_PROP_ID IS NOT NULL
THEN PropRel1.DRIVING_PROP_ID
END AS FINAL_DRIVING_ID
FROM
(SELECT RELATIONSHIP_ID,
OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER,
RELATIONSHIP_TYPE,
TARGET_TYPE,
DIRECTION_TYPE,
SRC_OBJ_TYPE,
SRC_OBJ_ID,
DEST_OBJ_TYPE,
DEST_OBJ_ID,
CREATED_BY,
CREATION_DATE,
LAST_UPDATED_BY,
LAST_UPDATE_DATE,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'PROPOSAL'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'REQUIREMENT')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'REQUIREMENT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'PROPOSAL')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS DERIVED_REQUIREMENT_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'PROPOSAL'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'CONCEPT')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'CONCEPT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'PROPOSAL')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS DERIVED_CONCEPT_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'PROPOSAL'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'IDEA')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'IDEA'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'PROPOSAL')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS DERIVED_IDEA_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'PROPOSAL'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'REQUIREMENT_LINE_ITEM')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'REQUIREMENT_LINE_ITEM'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'PROPOSAL')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS DERIVED_REQUIREMENT_LINE_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'PROPOSAL'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'COMPONENT')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'COMPONENT'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'PROPOSAL')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS DERIVED_COMPONENT_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type = 'PROPOSAL'
AND AR.dest_obj_type != 'PROPOSAL')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type != 'PROPOSAL'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'PROPOSAL')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
END AS DRIVING_PROP_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type = 'PROPOSAL'
AND AR.dest_obj_type != 'PROPOSAL')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type!= 'PROPOSAL'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'PROPOSAL')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
END AS derived_PROP_ID
FROM ACA_CS_RELATIONSHIP AR
WHERE SRC_OBJ_TYPE = 'PROPOSAL'
OR DEST_OBJ_TYPE = 'PROPOSAL'
) PropRel1,
(SELECT RELATIONSHIP_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'PROPOSAL'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'PROPOSAL')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
END AS derived_PROP_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'PROPOSAL'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'PROPOSAL')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS DRIVING_PROP_ID
FROM ACA_CS_RELATIONSHIP AR
WHERE SRC_OBJ_TYPE = 'PROPOSAL'
OR DEST_OBJ_TYPE = 'PROPOSAL'
UNION
SELECT RELATIONSHIP_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'PROPOSAL'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'PROPOSAL')
THEN AR.src_obj_id
END AS derived_PROP_ID,
CASE
WHEN (AR.src_obj_type= 'PROPOSAL'
AND AR.dest_obj_type = 'PROPOSAL')
THEN AR.dest_obj_id
END AS DRIVING_PROP_ID
FROM ACA_CS_RELATIONSHIP AR
WHERE SRC_OBJ_TYPE = 'PROPOSAL'
OR DEST_OBJ_TYPE = 'PROPOSAL'
) PropRel2
WHERE PropRel1.RELATIONSHIP_ID = PropRel2.RELATIONSHIP_ID
UNION ALL
SELECT poa.object_association_id AS relationship_id,
poa.object_version_number AS object_version_number,
NULL AS relationship_type,
NULL AS target_type,
NULL AS direction_type,
poa.object_type AS src_obj_type,
poa.object_id AS src_obj_id,
poa.associated_object_type AS dest_obj_type,
poa.associated_object_id AS dest_obj_id,
poa.created_by AS created_by,
poa.creation_date AS creation_date,
poa.last_updated_by AS last_updated_by,
poa.last_update_date AS last_update_date,
NULL AS derived_requirement_id,
NULL AS derived_concept_id,
NULL AS derived_idea_id,
NULL AS derived_requirement_line_id,
NULL AS derived_component_id,
pel.project_id AS derived_project_id,
poa.object_id AS derived_task_id,
poa.associated_object_id AS final_derived_id,
poa.associated_object_id AS final_driving_id
FROM
(SELECT *
FROM fusion.pje_object_associations
WHERE associated_object_sub_type_id IN
(SELECT DELIVERABLE_TYPE_ID
FROM PJE_DELIVERABLE_TYPES_VL PROPOSALCLASS
WHERE PROPOSALCLASS.DELIVERABLE_TYPE_CLASS='PLM_PROPOSAL'
)
) poa,
pjf_proj_elements_b pel
WHERE pel.proj_element_id=poa.object_id

objects.name: ACD_RESOURCE_MONTH_V
objects.query:
SELECT
RES.RESOURCE_ID,
RN,
RES.PRODUCT_PROPOSAL_ID,
RES.RESOURCE_POOL,
RES.RESOURCE_STATUS,
RES.START_DATE,
RES.END_DATE,
RES.RESOURCE_CATEGORY,
RES.RESOURCE_HEADCOUNT HEAD_COUNT_MONTH,
ROUND (RES.RESOURCE_HEADCOUNT / 3, 4) HEAD_COUNT_QUARTER,
ROUND (RES.RESOURCE_HEADCOUNT / 12, 4) HEAD_COUNT_YEAR,
ADD_MONTHS (TRUNC (RES.START_DATE,'MM'), RN) MONTH,
TO_NUMBER (TO_CHAR (ADD_MONTHS(TRUNC(RES.START_DATE,'MM'), RN),'YYYYQMM')) CAL_MONTH
FROM ACD_RESOURCE RES,
(SELECT ROWNUM-1 RN
FROM FND_LOOKUP_VALUES
WHERE ROWNUM <=
(SELECT MAX (ROUND (MONTHS_BETWEEN(TRUNC(ADD_MONTHS(RES1.END_DATE,1), 'MM'), TRUNC(RES1.START_DATE)),0))
FROM ACD_RESOURCE RES1
)
)
WHERE MONTHS_BETWEEN(TRUNC(ADD_MONTHS(RES.END_DATE, 1),'MM'), TRUNC(RES.START_DATE,'MM')) > RN

objects.name: ACA_CS_CLASS_B
objects.description: Contains the list of business classes registered for use by the application. The class table represents the metadata for a business object in the system. That is, each business object is created from a class definition. The class table contains all class definitions for all class families. Base class definitions are no different than other class definitions. In fact, the only thing that denotes a class as a base class is that its parent class ID is set to null. That is, a base class has no parent. Classes are maintained as a hierarchy. That is, all classes except for base classes are derived from a parent class. This hierarchy introduces the possibility of inheritance. With inheritance, parent class definition information may be added to or overridden by a child class.

columns.name: DELETED_FLAG

columns.name: DISABLE_DATE
columns.comments: Optional. The date the class is no longer active. If left blank, then the class definition will not expire.

columns.name: OBJECT_CREATION_ALLOWED_FLAG
columns.comments: Yes/No Flag. Indicates if objects can be created from this class definition. This establishes whether a class is abstract (Flag=N; cannot be instantiated) or concrete (Flag=Y; can be instantiated). Class policy may dictate the required value for this field. Class policy will also determine if the customer may change this value.

columns.name: TRACK_HISTORY_FLAG
columns.comments: This is a yes/no flag which allows customers to control whether history on object's of the particular type should be tracked.

columns.name: CLASS_FAMILY_CODE

columns.name: CLASS_SUB_FAMILY_CODE

columns.name: PARENT_CLASS_ID

columns.name: CLASS_POLICY

Standard (no restrictions) ??? Abstract Only o Object Creation Allowed Flag must = N o Object Creation Allowed Flag is read only for customers ??? objects.name: ACA_CS_CLASS_FAMILY
objects.description: Contains the Business Class Families that any classes belong to. A Class Family is nothing more than a normalization of class definitions. It represents the metadata associated with all classes whose objects are stored in the same set of tables and are governed by the same entity object in the application. The term family simply signifies that the same application business logic is applied to all business objects in a set. That is, the business objects are not necessarily related to one another in the data, but they are related to one another in the application logic. The existence of this table keeps us from either repeating the same data for each class using it or using a sparse data matrix to only store the class metadata with a base class. One advantage to factoring the metadata out into a separate table, it allows a class family to have more than one base class while ensuring that the metadata for each base class remains the same. The Class Family table is also the table where Common Services groups can add named attributes which represent business logic parameters. These parameters are specified at the Class Family because they apply to all classes within a class family. When the application views a class definition, the Class Family is automatically joined with the class definition. One can think of the Class Family as a normalization of the Class definitions. Note: no official requirements for this type of business logic parameter has been communicated; for now we are simply offering the design for how Class Family business logic parameters would be implemented. This table is preloaded with seeded data. This table is not modified by customers.

columns.name: CLASS_FAMILY_CODE
columns.comments: Primary Key. This table uses the code as the primary key instead of a numerical ID. The reason for this choice is to allow easy lookup of class data by the family code rather than having to join with this table only for the lookup. The values for this column are maintained in FND_LOOKUPS under the ACA_CS_CLASS_FAMILY lookup type. This allows the class family names to be translated without having to provide an additional UI just to localize the family names.

objects.name: ACA_PD_ITEM_COST
objects.description: The PD Item Cost data model contains the following costs: * Item costs from the Costing System * Item costs entered by end users for Items without costs from the Costing System * Rolled up costs for sub-assemblies to Item assemblies. The PD Items Costs are accessible by Item ID / Revision ID. This allows each Item revision to have its own set of costs. Costs which come from the Costing System are applicable to all revisions for an Item.

columns.name: ITEM_COST_ID
columns.comments: Primary Key for this table. This can be used as the surrogate key.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: INVENTORY_ITEM_ID
columns.comments: Foreign key to the Item (PK on the egp_system_items_b) table. Note: The complete Item PK contains Organization. PD only uses a single Organization. For this reason, Organization has been omitted from the Item Cost table. Note: A special row is used in this table to determine the last time the data was retrieved from the Costing System. ???-1??? is used as the inventory_item_id for the special row.

columns.name: ORGANIZATION_ID
columns.comments: Foreign key to the Item's organization (PK on the egp_system_items_b) table. This represent's the customer's Master Organization which was in effect at the time the cost data was pulled in from the Costing System.

columns.name: IS_LEAF
columns.comments: This column indicates if the item the cost is associated with is either a Leaf Item or an Assembly Item. This column is used when evaluating (filtering) on the From_Revision and To_Revision columns. Leaf Items: Use both the From_Revision and To_Revision. Revision ranges do not overlap. If To_Revision is not specified, then the revision range is considered to be open-ended. Assembly Items: The From_Revision and To_Revision columns will contain the same value; therefore, the To_Revision may be omitted when filtering. Values: ??? 1 = Leaf Item ??? 0 = Assembly Item ??? -1 = Special Row ??? to be ignored when filtering

columns.name: FROM_REVISION
columns.comments: This column indicates the starting Revision in a revision range for a leaf item. This column contains the Revision of a specific revision for an assembly item. WHERE CLAUSE: (Is_Leaf = 1 AND From_Revision <= Revision) OR (Is_Leaf = 0 AND From_Revision = Revision) Alternatively (to avoid the OR): DECODE(Is_Leaf, 1, DECODE(SIGN(From_Revision - Revision), 1, ???NO_MATCH???, ???MATCH???), 0, DECODE(SIGN(From_Revision - Revision), 0, ???MATCH???, ???NO_MATCH???), ???NO_MATCH???) = ???MATCH???

columns.name: TO_REVISION
columns.comments: This column indicates the ending Revision in a revision range for a leaf item. Revision ranges may be open ended (i.e. To_Revisoon = null). This column contains the Revision of a specific revision for an assembly item. WHERE CLAUSE: (Is_Leaf = 1 AND NVL(To_Revision, Revision) >= Revision) OR (Is_Leaf = 0) Alternatively (to avoid the OR): DECODE(Is_Leaf, 1, DECODE(SIGN(NVL(To_Revision, Revision) - Revision), -1, ???NO_MATCH???, ???MATCH???), 0, ???MATCH???, ???NO_MATCH???) = ???MATCH???

columns.name: LAST_COST_EXTRACT_DATE
columns.comments: This is the date the cost for the current row was last extracted from the Costing System. Note: This column is only for the special row or the rows which have been updated with data from the Costing System.

columns.name: LAST_ROLLUP_DATE
columns.comments: This is the date the rollup costs for the Item assembly were last calculated. This date would only be specified for Items which represent assemblies (top level or sub assemblies). This date is not set for assembly leaf items.

columns.name: COST_SOURCE
columns.comments: This column indicates where the costing data for the Item came from. Values: * Z = special row which tracks when the Retrieve Costing System Costs process was last run. * C = Costing System * P = PD Edit Item

columns.name: INVENTORY_ORG_ID
columns.comments: This is the organization ID used to request cost information from the Costing System. If multiple organization IDs are used to request cost information for the same item, then the inventory organization is the organization for which the cost information was actually retrieved.

columns.name: CURRENCY_CODE
columns.comments: This is the currency of the cost information stored on the row. This currency is the currency requested from the Costing System.

columns.name: MATERIAL_COST
columns.comments: The material cost to use for the Item. It would come from the Costing System or user-entered in PD Edit Item. This is a cost that is directly associated with the Item ID. Note: As of this design, material costs would only be tracked for assembly leaf items, i.e. items without sub-structures.

columns.name: OVERHEAD_COST
columns.comments: The overhead cost to use for the Item. It would come from the Costing System or user-entered in PD Edit Item. This is a cost that is directly associated with the Item ID. Note: As of this design, overhead costs would only be tracked for assembly items, i.e. items with sub-structures.

columns.name: ROLLUP_MATERIAL_COST
columns.comments: The sum of the material costs times the quantities needed for the items that make up the assembly Item. These costs can be considered indirect costs because their origin does not come directly from this Item???s Item ID.

columns.name: ROLLUP_OVERHEAD_COST
columns.comments: The sum of the overhead costs times the quantities needed for the items that make up the assembly Item. These costs can be considered indirect costs because their origin does not come directly from this Item???s Item ID.

columns.name: INCOMPLETE_COST_CNT
columns.comments: The number of items, leaf or assembly, directly tied to the Item Revision for the cost row which do not have costs or complete costs. Leaf items will either have a cost or not. Assembly item???s costs will either be complete or incomplete.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.comments: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: CONFLICT_ID
columns.comments: Disconnected Mobile: this value is used to guarantee the uniqueness of the row when duplicates are created in different databases (i.e. mobile databases or the server).

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.comments: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.comments: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.comments: Disconnected Mobile: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row. This value is different from LAST_UPDATE_DATE if the update originally happened in a different database (i.e. a different mobile database or the server).

columns.name: JOB_DEFINITION_PACKAGE

objects.name: ACA_AUTO_SEQ_METADATA_VL
objects.query:
SELECT
B.AUTO_SEQ_METADATA_ID AUTO_SEQ_METADATA_ID,
B.OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER,
B.AUTO_SEQ_CLASS_ID AUTO_SEQ_CLASS_ID,
B.AUTO_SEQ_CODE AUTO_SEQ_CODE,
B.STARTING_NUMBER STARTING_NUMBER,
B.INCREMENT_BY INCREMENT_BY,
B.PREFIX PREFIX,
B.SUFFIX SUFFIX,
B.MAXIMUM_ATTEMPTS MAXIMUM_ATTEMPTS,
B.IS_SEEDED IS_SEEDED,
TL.DESCRIPTION DESCRIPTION,
B.CREATED_BY CREATED_BY,
B.CREATION_DATE CREATION_DATE,
B.LAST_UPDATED_BY LAST_UPDATED_BY,
B.LAST_UPDATE_DATE LAST_UPDATE_DATE,
B.LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
FROM
ACA_AUTO_SEQ_METADATA_B B,
ACA_AUTO_SEQ_METADATA_TL TL
WHERE
B.AUTO_SEQ_METADATA_ID = TL.AUTO_SEQ_METADATA_ID AND TL.LANGUAGE = USERENV('LANG')

objects.name: VCS_PREVIOUS_CYCLE_ENTRY_V
objects.query:
SELECT
PreviousCycleDetailsEO.bucket_id AS PREVIOUS_BUCKET_ID,
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.INVENTORY_ITEM_ID ,
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.IS_CURRENT_FLAG AS ENTRY_CURRENT_FLAG,
PreviousCycleDetailsEO.entry_detail_id previous_entry_detail_id,
PreviousCycleDetailsEO.QUANTITY AS PREVIOUS_QUANTITY,
PreviousCycleDetailsEO.RESPONSE_QUANTITY AS PREVIOUS_RESPONSE_QUANTITY,
PreviousCycleDetailsEO.RESPONSE_QUANTITY_UOM AS PREVIOUS_RESPONSE_QUANTITY_UOM,
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.entry_id as CurrentEntryID,
PreviousCycleEntriesEO.entry_id as PreviousEntryID,
PreviousCycleEntriesEO.primary_uom_code AS PREVIOUS_PRIMARY_UOM_CODE,
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.SHIP_TO_ID,
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.INVENTORY_ITEM_ORG_ID,
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.PUBLISHED_DATE,
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.COMMIT_DATE,
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.LAST_UPDATE_DATE as ENTRY_LAST_UPDATE_DATE,
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.LAST_UPDATED_BY,
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN AS ENTRY_LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN,
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER AS OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER_ENT,
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.SHIP_FROM_ID,
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.ORCH_CORRELATION_CODE
FROM
VCS_COLLAB_ENT CurrentCycleEntriesEO
LEFT JOIN VCS_COLLAB_ENT PreviousCycleEntriesEO ON CurrentCycleEntriesEO.INVENTORY_ITEM_ID = PreviousCycleEntriesEO.INVENTORY_ITEM_ID AND
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.INVENTORY_ITEM_ORG_ID = PreviousCycleEntriesEO.INVENTORY_ITEM_ORG_ID AND
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.SHIP_TO_ID = PreviousCycleEntriesEO.SHIP_TO_ID AND
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.SHIP_FROM_ID = PreviousCycleEntriesEO.SHIP_FROM_ID AND
CurrentCycleEntriesEO.COLLAB_SOURCE_ID = PreviousCycleEntriesEO.COLLAB_SOURCE_ID AND
PreviousCycleEntriesEO.IS_CURRENT_FLAG = 'N'
LEFT JOIN VCS_PLANNING_SCH_DETAILS PreviousCycleDetailsEO ON PreviousCycleDetailsEO.COLLAB_ENTRY_ID =PreviousCycleEntriesEO.entry_id AND
PreviousCycleDetailsEO.IS_CURRENT_FLAG = 'Y'
WHERE CurrentCycleEntriesEO.IS_CURRENT_FLAG = 'Y'
